bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第172卷 卷第一百七十二 。

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 172, Volume 172 in words.
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 172.

sentences.zh: 【陳紀六】 起旃蒙協洽，盡柔兆涒灘，凡二年。

translations.literal: [Chen Records 6] From Zhanmeng Xieqia through Rouzhao Tuntan; two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Chen Records 6] From Zhanmeng Xieqia through Rouzhao Tuntan—two years in all.

sentences.zh: 高宗宣皇帝中之上太建七年（乙未，公元五七五年） 。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan of Chen, middle reign, upper part: Taikjian year 7 (yiwei, AD 575).
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan of Chen, middle reign, upper part: Taikjian year 7 (yiwei, AD 575).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛未，上祀南郊。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on xinwei, the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on xinwei, the Chen emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，周主如同州。

translations.literal: On guiyou, the Zhou ruler went to Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, the Zhou emperor went to Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，左衛將軍樊毅克潼州。

translations.literal: On yihai, Left Guard General Fan Yi captured Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Chen Left Guard General Fan Yi captured Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 齊主還鄴。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler returned to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi emperor returned to Ye.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，上祀北郊。

translations.literal: On xinsi, the emperor sacrificed at the northern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, the Chen emperor sacrificed at the northern suburb.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙戌朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the bingxu new moon, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the bingxu new moon, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 戊申，樊毅克下邳、高柵等六城。

translations.literal: On wushen, Fan Yi captured Xiapi, Gaozha, and six other cities.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Fan Yi captured Xiapi, Gaozha, and six other cities.

sentences.zh: 齊主言語澀吶，不喜見朝士，自非寵私暱狎，未嘗交語。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler's speech was halting and tongue-tied; he disliked seeing court officials, and unless they were favorites with whom he was intimate, he never exchanged words with them.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi emperor spoke haltingly and disliked receiving court officials; except for intimate favorites, he never spoke with them at all.

sentences.zh: 性懦，不堪人視，雖三公、令、錄奏事，莫得仰視，皆略陳大指，驚走而出。

translations.literal: By nature timid, he could not bear to be looked at; even when the Three Excellencies, ministers, and recorders reported affairs, they might not look up at him—all briefly stated the main points, then fled out in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Timid by nature, he could not bear anyone's gaze; even when the Three Excellencies, ministers, and recorders reported business, they were forbidden to look up. They would state only the gist and flee out in alarm.

sentences.zh: 承世祖奢泰之餘，以為帝王當然，後宮皆寶衣玉食，一裙之費，至直萬匹。

translations.literal: Inheriting the extravagance and luxury left by Emperor Shizu, he took it as what an emperor ought to be; the inner palace all wore jeweled robes and jade fare, and the cost of a single skirt reached as much as ten thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Taking over the extravagance of his predecessor Gao Yang, he assumed such excess was only fitting for an emperor. The inner palace dressed in jeweled robes and feasted on jade fare; a single skirt could cost ten thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 競為新巧，朝衣夕弊。

translations.literal: They vied in novelties and ingenuity; garments worn in the morning were cast aside by evening.
translations.idiomatic: They vied in novel designs; a garment worn in the morning was discarded by evening.

sentences.zh: 盛修宮苑，窮極壯麗。

translations.literal: Palaces and parks were built on a grand scale, pushed to the utmost splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Palaces and parks were built on a grand scale, pushed to the utmost splendor.

sentences.zh: 所好不常，數毀又復。

translations.literal: What he favored did not last; again and again he demolished and rebuilt.
translations.idiomatic: His tastes shifted constantly; again and again he tore down what he had just built and rebuilt anew.

sentences.zh: 百工土木，無時休息，夜則然火照作，寒則以湯為泥。

translations.literal: Craftsmen and earthworks had no rest; at night they lit fires to work by, and in cold weather used hot broth as mortar.
translations.idiomatic: Artisans and laborers had no rest; at night fires were lit so work could continue, and in cold weather hot broth was used as mortar.

sentences.zh: 鑿晉陽西山為大像，一夜然油萬盆，光照宮中。

translations.literal: He carved the western hills of Jinyang into a great image; in one night ten thousand basins of oil were burned, and the light filled the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He had the western hills of Jinyang carved into a colossal Buddha image; in a single night ten thousand basins of oil were burned, and the light filled the palace.

sentences.zh: 每有災異寇盜，不自貶損，唯多設齋，以為修德。

translations.literal: Whenever there were omens, calamities, or bandits, he did not humble himself but only set up many vegetarian feasts, taking this as cultivating virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever omens, disasters, or banditry occurred, he never blamed himself but only ordered more Buddhist feasts, imagining this was cultivating virtue.

sentences.zh: 好自彈琵琶，為《無愁》之曲，近侍和之者以百數，民間謂之「無愁天子」。

translations.literal: He loved to play the pipa himself and composed the tune "Without Sorrow"; those among his close attendants who harmonized with him numbered in the hundreds, and the people called him "the Carefree Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: He loved to play the pipa himself and composed the tune "Without Sorrow"; hundreds of close attendants sang along, and the people called him "the Carefree Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 於華林園立貧兒村，帝自衣藍縷之服，行乞其間為樂。

translations.literal: In Hualin Park he set up a Village of Poor Boys; the emperor himself wore ragged blue clothes and begged there for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: In Hualin Park he built a "Village of Beggar Boys," donned ragged blue clothes himself, and went begging there for amusement.

sentences.zh: 又寫築西鄙諸城，使人衣黑衣攻之，帝自帥內參拒鬥。

translations.literal: He also laid out models of the western border fortresses; men in black clothes were made to attack them, and the emperor himself led the inner attendants to resist and fight.
translations.idiomatic: He also had models built of the western frontier fortresses, sent men in black to attack them, and led the palace attendants himself in mock defense.

sentences.zh: 寵任陸令萱、穆提婆、高阿那肱、韓長鸞等宰制朝政，宦官鄧長顒、陳德信、胡兒何洪珍等並參預機權，各引親黨，超居顯位。

translations.literal: He favored and entrusted Lu Lingxuan, Mu Tipo, Gao Anagong, Han Changluan, and others to dominate court affairs; eunuchs Deng Changying, Chen Dexin, the Hu boy He Hongzhen, and others all shared in power, each advancing their kin to leap into eminent posts.
translations.idiomatic: He entrusted Lu Lingxuan, Mu Tipo, Gao Anagong, Han Changluan, and others to dominate the government; eunuchs Deng Changying, Chen Dexin, the Hu attendant He Hongzhen, and others all shared power, each promoting kin to exalted office.

sentences.zh: 官由財進，獄以賄成，競為奸諂，蠹政害民。

translations.literal: Office came through wealth, lawsuits through bribes; they vied in treachery and flattery, corrupting government and harming the people.
translations.idiomatic: Offices were bought with money and lawsuits settled with bribes; they vied in treachery and flattery, ruining government and harming the people.

sentences.zh: 舊蒼頭劉桃枝等皆開府封王，其餘宦官、胡兒、歌舞人、見鬼人、官奴婢等濫得富貴者，殆將萬數，庶姓封王者以百數，開府千餘人，儀同無數，領軍一時至二十人，侍中、中常侍數十人，乃至狗、馬及鷹亦有儀同、郡君之號，有鬥雞，號開府，皆食其干祿。

translations.literal: Former servants such as Liu Taozhi all received grand-marshal offices and princely enfeoffment; other eunuchs, Hu boys, singers and dancers, spirit-seers, official slave-girls, and the like who wantonly gained wealth and rank nearly reached ten thousand. Commoners enfeoffed as kings numbered in the hundreds; grand-marshal offices exceeded a thousand, honorary peers beyond count; at one time there were as many as twenty commanders-in-chief and dozens of palace attendants and chief eunuchs—even dogs, horses, and hawks bore honorary-peer and district-lady titles; there was a fighting cock styled Grand Marshal, and all drew state stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Former servants such as Liu Taozhi were all made grand marshals and enfeoffed as kings; eunuchs, Hu attendants, performers, spirit-mediums, palace slaves, and the like who gained wealth and rank by the thousand nearly numbered ten thousand. Commoners enfeoffed as kings ran to the hundreds; over a thousand held grand-marshal titles and honorary-peer ranks beyond counting. At one time there were twenty commanders-in-chief and dozens of palace attendants and chief eunuchs—even dogs, horses, and hawks bore honorary-peer and district-lady titles; a fighting cock was styled Grand Marshal, and all drew state stipends.

sentences.zh: 諸嬖倖朝夕娛侍左右，一戲之賞，動逾巨萬。

translations.literal: The various favorites amused him morning and evening at his side; a single reward for a jest often exceeded tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Favorites entertained him day and night at his side; a single reward for a jest often exceeded tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 既而府藏空竭，乃賜二三郡或六七縣，使之賣官取直。

translations.literal: When the treasury was emptied, he bestowed two or three commanderies or six or seven counties and had favorites sell offices for cash.
translations.idiomatic: When the treasury was exhausted, he granted favorites two or three commanderies or six or seven counties and let them sell offices for cash.

sentences.zh: 由是為守令者，率皆富商大賈，競為貪縱，賦繁役重，民不聊生。

translations.literal: Hence those who became prefects and magistrates were mostly great merchants and traders, who vied in greed and license; taxes were heavy and corvée burdens severe, and the people could not live.
translations.idiomatic: Hence prefects and magistrates were mostly wealthy merchants who vied in greed; taxes and corvée grew crushing, and the people could barely survive.

sentences.zh: 周高祖謀伐齊，命邊鎮益儲偫，加戍卒；

translations.literal: Northern Zhou's Emperor Wu planned to attack Qi and ordered the border garrisons to increase stored provisions and add garrison troops;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou planned to attack Qi and ordered the border garrisons to stock more provisions and add troops;

sentences.zh: 齊人聞之，亦增修守禦。

translations.literal: when the Qi heard of it, they too strengthened defenses.
translations.idiomatic: when the Qi heard of this, they too strengthened their defenses.

sentences.zh: 柱國於翼諫曰：「疆場相侵，互有勝負，徒損兵儲，無益大計。

translations.literal: Pillar of State Yu Yi remonstrated, saying: "Border clashes with mutual victories and defeats only waste troops and stores and do no good to the great plan.
translations.idiomatic: Pillar of State Yu Yi remonstrated, saying, "Border skirmishes with alternating victories only waste troops and stores and advance no great design.

sentences.zh: 不如解嚴繼好，使彼懈而無備，然後乘間，出其不意，一舉可取也。

translations.literal: Better to stand down the armies and renew friendship, so that they relax and are unguarded; then seize the moment, strike where they do not expect, and take them in one move."
translations.idiomatic: Better to stand the armies down and renew friendly ties so they relax their guard; then seize the moment, strike where they do not expect, and take them at one blow."

sentences.zh: 」周主從之。

translations.literal: " The Zhou ruler followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The Zhou emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 韋孝寬上疏陳三策。

translations.literal: Wei Xiaokuan submitted a memorial setting forth three strategies.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaokuan submitted a memorial presenting three strategies.

sentences.zh: 其一曰：「臣在邊積年，頗見間隙，不因際會，難以成功。

translations.literal: The first says: "Your servant has spent many years on the frontier and has seen openings; without seizing the occasion, success is hard.
translations.idiomatic: The first said, "Your servant has spent many years on the frontier and has seen openings; without seizing the moment, success is hard.

sentences.zh: 是以往歲出軍，徒有勞費，功績不立，由失機會。

translations.literal: Hence when armies went out in past years, there was only toil and expense and no achievement established, because the opportunity was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Hence past campaigns brought only toil and expense with no achievement, because the opportunity was missed.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 長淮之南，舊為沃土，陳氏以破亡餘燼，猶能一舉平之；

translations.literal: South of the Long Huai was once fertile land; Chen, though the embers of a ruined state, could still level it in one stroke;
translations.idiomatic: South of the Long Huai was once fertile land; Chen, though barely surviving ruin, could still conquer it in one stroke;

sentences.zh: 齊人歷年赴救，喪敗而返。

translations.literal: the Qi for years rushed to the rescue and returned in defeat and loss.
translations.idiomatic: the Qi for years rushed to relieve it and returned defeated.

sentences.zh: 內離外叛，計盡力窮，讎敵有釁，不可失也。

translations.literal: Within there is estrangement and without rebellion; plans are exhausted and strength spent—the foe shows a crack that must not be missed.
translations.idiomatic: Within they are divided and without they face rebellion; plans are exhausted and strength spent—the enemy shows a crack that must not be missed.

sentences.zh: 今大軍若出軹關，方軌而進，兼與陳氏共為掎角，並令廣州義旅出自三鴉，又募山南驍銳，沿河而下，復遣北山稽胡，絕其並、晉之路。

translations.literal: Now if the great army issues from Zhiguan and advances in parallel columns, jointly with Chen forming pincers, and Guangzhou volunteers are sent out from Sanya, while fierce troops south of the mountains are recruited to descend along the river, and Northern Mountain Jie Hu are dispatched to cut the roads through Bing and Jin—
translations.idiomatic: Now if the main army issues from Zhiguan and advances in parallel columns, coordinating pincers with Chen, while Guangzhou volunteers strike from Sanya, fierce troops south of the mountains descend the river, and Northern Mountain Jie Hu cut the roads through Bing and Jin—

sentences.zh: 凡此諸軍，仍令各募關、河之外勁勇之士，厚其爵賞，使為前驅。

translations.literal: for all these armies, let each also recruit stalwart warriors beyond the passes and rivers, enrich their ranks and rewards, and make them vanguards.
translations.idiomatic: let each of these forces also recruit stalwart warriors beyond the passes and rivers, enrich their rewards, and use them as vanguards.

sentences.zh: 岳動川移，雷駭電激，百道俱進，並趨虜庭。

translations.literal: Mountains will shake and rivers shift, thunder will startle and lightning flash; a hundred routes will advance together and all press on the barbarian court.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains will shake and rivers shift like thunder and lightning; a hundred routes will advance together upon the enemy capital.

sentences.zh: 必當望旗奔潰，所向摧殄，一戎大定，實在此機。

translations.literal: They will surely flee at sight of banners and be destroyed wherever we turn; one campaign will settle all—truly this is the moment."
translations.idiomatic: They will surely flee at sight of our banners and be crushed wherever we turn; one campaign will settle all—truly this is the moment."

sentences.zh: 其二曰：「若國家更為後圖，未即大舉，宜與陳人分其兵勢。

translations.literal: The second says: "If the state plans further ahead and does not launch a great campaign at once, it should with Chen divide their military strength.
translations.idiomatic: The second said, "If the state plans further ahead and does not launch a great campaign at once, it should work with Chen to divide their military strength.

sentences.zh: 三鴉以北，萬春以南，廣事屯田，預為貯積，募其驍悍，立為部伍。

translations.literal: North of Sanya and south of Wanchun, widely practice garrison farming, store provisions in advance, recruit their fierce and bold, and organize them into units.
translations.idiomatic: North of Sanya and south of Wanchun, expand garrison farming, stock provisions in advance, recruit fierce men, and organize them into units.

sentences.zh: 彼既東南有敵，戎馬相持，我出奇兵，破其疆場。

translations.literal: Since they already have an enemy in the southeast and their armies are tied down, we send surprise troops and break their borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: Since they already face an enemy in the southeast and their armies are tied down, we send surprise troops and ravage their borderlands.

sentences.zh: 彼若興師赴援，我則堅壁清野，待其去遠，還復出師。

translations.literal: If they raise armies to rescue, we fortify walls and clear the countryside, wait until they are far off, then march out again.
translations.idiomatic: If they march to relieve, we fortify and clear the countryside, wait until they are far away, then strike again.

sentences.zh: 常以邊外之軍，引其腹心之眾。

translations.literal: Constantly use armies on the outer borders to draw their core forces.
translations.idiomatic: Constantly use frontier forces to draw off their core armies.

sentences.zh: 我無宿舂之費，彼有奔命之勞，一二年中，必自離叛。

translations.literal: We bear no cost of overnight milling; they have the toil of rushing to arms—in one or two years they will surely split and rebel of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: We bear no cost of overnight supply; they exhaust themselves rushing to arms—in one or two years they will split and rebel on their own.

sentences.zh: 且齊氏昏暴，政出多門，鬻獄賣官，唯利是視，荒淫酒色，忌害忠良，闔境嗷然，不勝其弊。

translations.literal: Moreover the Qi are benighted and cruel; government issues from many gates; they sell lawsuits and offices and look only to profit; they waste themselves in wine and women and envy and harm the loyal; the whole realm groans and cannot bear their abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Qi is benighted and cruel; power is scattered; lawsuits and offices are sold for profit; the court drowns in wine and women and destroys the loyal; the whole realm groans under abuses it cannot bear.

sentences.zh: 以此而觀，覆亡可待，然後乘間電掃，事等摧枯。

translations.literal: Viewed thus, collapse waits only for time; then seize the moment like a lightning sweep, a matter like breaking dry wood."
translations.idiomatic: Viewed thus, collapse is only a matter of time; then seize the moment like a lightning sweep, as easy as snapping dry wood."

sentences.zh: 其三曰：「昔勾踐亡吳，尚期十載；

translations.literal: The third says: "In old times Goujian destroyed Wu yet still allowed ten years;
translations.idiomatic: The third said, "In old times Goujian destroyed Wu yet allowed ten years;

sentences.zh: 武王取紂，猶煩再舉。

translations.literal: King Wu took Zhou yet still needed two campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu overthrew Zhou yet still needed two campaigns.

sentences.zh: 今若更存遵養，且復相時，臣謂宜還崇鄰好，申其盟約，安民和眾，通商惠工，蓄銳養威，觀釁而動。

translations.literal: If now we further preserve nurturing and again watch the times, your servant holds we should honor neighborly friendship, renew the covenant, settle the people and harmonize the masses, open trade and benefit craftsmen, store sharpness and nurture might, and move when we see a crack.
translations.idiomatic: If we now preserve strength and watch the times, your servant holds we should honor neighborly ties, renew treaties, settle the people, open trade, store strength, and strike when a crack appears.

sentences.zh: 斯乃長策遠馭，坐自兼併也。

translations.literal: This is the long plan and distant control—sitting to annex of itself."
translations.idiomatic: This is the long-term strategy—annexation achieved while seated."

sentences.zh: 」書奏，周主引開府儀同三司伊婁謙入內殿，從容謂曰：「朕欲用兵，何者為先？

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, the Zhou ruler summoned Grand Marshal of the Palace with Equal Third Rank Yilou Qian into the inner hall and calmly said: "I wish to use the army—which target should come first?
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial arrived, the Zhou emperor summoned Grand Marshal Yilou Qian to the inner hall and said calmly, "I wish to use the army—which target should come first?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「齊氏沈溺倡優，耽昏麴薛。

translations.literal: " He replied: "The Qi are sunk in entertainers and actors, lost in wine and women.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Qi is sunk in entertainers and actors, lost in wine and women.

sentences.zh: 其折衝之將斛律明月，已斃於讒口。

translations.literal: Their general who met the foe, Hulu Guangyue, has already been killed by slander.
translations.idiomatic: Their champion Hulu Guangyue has already been destroyed by slander.

sentences.zh: 上下離心，道路以目。

translations.literal: Above and below are estranged; people exchange glances in the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Court and people are estranged; men exchange fearful glances in the streets.

sentences.zh: 此易取也。

translations.literal: This is easy to take."
translations.idiomatic: Qi is easy to take."

sentences.zh: 」帝大笑。

translations.literal: " The emperor laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor laughed heartily.

sentences.zh: 三月，丙辰，使謙與小司寇元衛聘於齊以觀釁。

translations.literal: In the third month, on bingchen, he sent Qian and Junior Minister of Justice Yuan Wei as envoys to Qi to observe for cracks.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingchen, he sent Qian and Junior Minister of Justice Yuan Wei as envoys to Qi to probe for weakness.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，周主還長安。

translations.literal: On bingyin, the Zhou ruler returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, the Zhou emperor returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲午，上享太廟。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jiawu, the emperor offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on jiawu, the Chen emperor offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 監豫州陳桃根得青牛，獻之，詔遣還民。

translations.literal: Supervisor of Yuzhou Chen Taogen obtained a blue ox and presented it; an edict ordered it returned to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor of Yuzhou Chen Taogen obtained a blue ox and presented it; an edict ordered it returned to the people.

sentences.zh: 又表上織成羅文錦被各二百首，詔於雲龍門外焚之。

translations.literal: He also memorialized presenting two hundred each of woven patterned brocade coverlets; an edict ordered them burned outside the Cloud Dragon Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He also presented two hundred each of woven brocade coverlets; an edict ordered them burned outside the Cloud Dragon Gate.

sentences.zh: 庚子，齊以中書監陽休之為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Qi appointed Palace Secretariat Supervisor Yang Xiuzhi Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Northern Qi appointed Palace Secretariat Supervisor Yang Xiuzhi Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬辰，以尚書右僕射王瑒為左僕射。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on renchen, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Wang Chang was made Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renchen, Chen Right Vice Director Wang Chang was made Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，齊主如晉陽。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, the Qi ruler went to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, the Northern Qi emperor went to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙戌，周主如雲陽宮。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingxu, the Zhou ruler went to the Cloud Yang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingxu, the Zhou emperor went to the Cloud Yang Palace.

sentences.zh: 大將軍楊堅姿相奇偉。

translations.literal: Grand General Yang Jian's bearing and appearance were extraordinarily imposing.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Yang Jian's bearing and appearance were extraordinarily imposing.

sentences.zh: 畿伯下大夫長安來和嘗謂堅曰：「公眼如曙星，無所不照，當王有天下，願忍誅殺。

translations.literal: Jibo Lower Grandee of Chang'an Lai He once said to Jian: "My lord's eyes are like dawn stars that shine on all things; you are destined to rule the realm—please bear to kill sparingly."
translations.idiomatic: Jibo Lower Grandee Lai He of Chang'an once told Jian, "My lord's eyes are like dawn stars that miss nothing; you are destined to rule the realm—please restrain yourself in killing."

sentences.zh: 周主待堅素厚，齊王憲言於帝曰：「普六茹堅，相貌非常，臣每見之，不覺自失。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler had long treated Jian generously; Prince of Qi Xian said to the emperor: "Puliu Jian's appearance is extraordinary; whenever your servant sees him, he cannot help losing himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor had long favored Jian; Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian told him, "Puliu Jian's appearance is extraordinary; whenever I see him I lose myself.

sentences.zh: 恐非人下，請早除之！

translations.literal: I fear he is not one to serve under others—please remove him early!"
translations.idiomatic: I fear he is not meant to serve another—please eliminate him early!"

sentences.zh: 」帝亦疑之，以問來和。

translations.literal: " The emperor also grew suspicious and questioned Lai He.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor also grew suspicious and questioned Lai He.

sentences.zh: 和詭對曰：「隨公止是守節人，可鎮一方。

translations.literal: He answered evasively: "Duke Sui is only a man who keeps his integrity; he can guard one region.
translations.idiomatic: He answered evasively, "Duke Sui is only a man of integrity; he can guard one region.

sentences.zh: 若為將領，陳無不破。

translations.literal: If made a commander, Chen would be nowhere he did not break."
translations.idiomatic: As a commander, he would smash every Chen force he met."

sentences.zh: 丁卯，周主還長安。

translations.literal: On dingmao, the Zhou ruler returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, the Zhou emperor returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 先是，周主獨與齊王憲及內史王誼謀伐齊，又遣納言盧韞乘馹三詣安州總管於翼問策，餘人皆莫之知。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Zhou ruler alone with Prince of Qi Xian and Director of the Palace Secretariat Wang Yi plotted to attack Qi, and again sent Supervisor of Diverse Affairs Lu Yun to ride post relays three times to go to Anzhou Inspector-General Yu Yi to inquire strategy; the rest all did not know it.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, the Zhou emperor secretly planned to attack Qi together only with Prince Xian of Qi and Wang Yi, Director of the Palace Secretariat. He also sent Lu Yun, Supervisor of Diverse Affairs, on post relays three times to consult Yu Yi, Inspector-General of Anzhou, on strategy. No one else knew of this.

sentences.zh: 丙子，始召大將軍以上於大德殿告之。

translations.literal: On bingzi, he first summoned grand generals and above to the Dade Hall and informed them.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, he first summoned all officers of grand general rank and above to the Dade Hall and disclosed the plan.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，下詔伐齊，以柱國陳王純、滎陽公司消難、鄭公達奚震為前三軍總管，越王盛、周昌公侯莫陳崇、趙王招為後三軍總管。

translations.literal: On dingchou, an edict was issued to attack Qi; Pillar of State Chen Wang Chun, Xingyang Duke Sizixia, and Zheng Duke Daxizhen were appointed commanders-in-chief of the first, second, and third armies, and Yue Wang Sheng, Zhouchang Duke Houmochen Chong, and Zhao Wang Zhao were appointed commanders-in-chief of the fourth, fifth, and sixth armies.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, an edict was issued to attack Qi. Chen Wang Chun the Duke of Chen, Sizixia the Duke of Xingyang, and Daxizhen the Duke of Zheng were appointed commanders-in-chief of the first three armies; Yue Wang Sheng, Houmochen Chong the Duke of Zhouchang, and Zhao Wang Zhao were appointed commanders-in-chief of the rear three armies.

sentences.zh: 齊王憲帥眾二萬趨黎陽，隨公楊堅、廣寧公薛迥將舟師三萬自渭入河，梁公侯莫陳芮帥眾二萬守太行道，申公李穆帥眾三萬守河陽道，常山公於翼帥眾二萬出陳、汝。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Xian led twenty thousand troops toward Liyang; Duke of Sui Yang Jian and Duke of Guangning Xue Jiong commanded thirty thousand naval troops entering the river from the Wei; Duke of Liang Houmochen Rui led twenty thousand troops to guard the Taihang route; Duke of Shen Li Mu led thirty thousand troops to guard the Heyang route; Duke of Changshan Yu Yi led twenty thousand troops out toward Chen and Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Qi led twenty thousand troops toward Liyang. Duke of Sui Yang Jian and Duke of Guangning Xue Jiong commanded thirty thousand naval troops entering the river from the Wei. Duke of Liang Houmochen Rui led twenty thousand troops to guard the Taihang route. Duke of Shen Li Mu led thirty thousand troops to guard the Heyang route. Duke of Changshan Yu Yi led twenty thousand troops out toward Chen and Ru.

sentences.zh: 誼，盟之兄孫；

translations.literal: Yi was the elder brother's grandson of Meng;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi was the elder brother's grandson of Wang Meng;

sentences.zh: 震，武之子也。

translations.literal: Zhen was Wu's son.
translations.idiomatic: Daxizhen was the son of Daxi Wu.

sentences.zh: 周主將出河陽，內史上士宇文弼曰：「齊氏建國，於今累世；

translations.literal: As the Zhou ruler was about to advance from Heyang, Neishi Senior Clerk Yuwen Bi said: "The Qi house has established its state for many generations now;
translations.idiomatic: As the Zhou emperor was about to advance from Heyang, Neishi Senior Clerk Yuwen Bi said, "The Qi dynasty has been established for many generations now;

sentences.zh: 雖曰無道，籓鎮之任，尚有其人。

translations.literal: Though they are said to be without the Way, in the duties of frontier commands there are still capable men.
translations.idiomatic: Although they are said to be without the Way, in the duties of frontier commands there are still capable men.

sentences.zh: 今之出師，要須擇地。

translations.literal: For this present campaign, one must choose the ground.
translations.idiomatic: For the present campaign, it is essential to choose the ground carefully.

sentences.zh: 河陽衝要，精兵所聚，盡力攻圍，恐難得志。

translations.literal: Heyang is a strategic choke point where elite troops are gathered; if we exhaust ourselves attacking and besieging it, I fear we will find it hard to achieve our aim.
translations.idiomatic: Heyang is a strategic choke point where elite troops are concentrated; if we exhaust ourselves besieging it, I fear we will find it hard to achieve our aim.

sentences.zh: 如臣所見，出於汾曲，戍小山平，攻之易拔。

translations.literal: In my view, if we advance from Fenqu, the garrison hills are low and small, and attacking them will be easy to capture.
translations.idiomatic: As I see it, if we advance from Fenqu, the garrisons on the small hills are low and easy to storm and capture.

sentences.zh: 用武之地，莫過於此。

translations.literal: There is no place better than this to exert military force.
translations.idiomatic: There is no better place than this to exert military force.

sentences.zh: 」民部中大夫天水趙煚曰：「河南、洛陽，四面受敵，縱得之，不可以守。

translations.literal: " Minbu Central Grandee Zhao Jiong of Tianshui said: "Henan and Luoyang are exposed to enemy attack on all four sides; even if we take them, we cannot hold them.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhao Jiong, Central Grandee of the Ministry of the People from Tianshui, said, "Henan and Luoyang are exposed to attack on all sides; even if we take them, we cannot hold them.

sentences.zh: 請從河北直指太原，傾其巢穴，可一舉而定。

translations.literal: I ask that we advance from north of the River straight at Taiyuan and topple their nest; in one stroke it can be settled.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that we advance from north of the Yellow River straight toward Taiyuan and strike at their nest; in one blow we can settle the matter.

sentences.zh: 」遂伯下大夫鮑宏曰：「我強齊弱，我治齊亂，何憂不克！

translations.literal: " Suibo Lower Grandee Bao Hong said: "We are strong and Qi is weak; we are well governed and Qi is in turmoil—what worry that we will not conquer!
translations.idiomatic: " Bao Hong, Lower Grandee of Suibo, said, "We are strong and Qi is weak; we are well governed and Qi is in turmoil—why worry that we will not succeed!

sentences.zh: 但先帝往日屢出洛陽，彼既有備，每用不捷。

translations.literal: But the former emperor in past days repeatedly marched out against Luoyang; since they already had preparations, each time it was not successful.
translations.idiomatic: But the former emperor in past times repeatedly marched on Luoyang; the enemy already had defenses ready, and each time the result was not victorious.

sentences.zh: 如臣計者，進兵汾、潞，直掩晉陽，出其不虞，似為上策。

translations.literal: According to my plan, advance troops through Fen and Lu, directly strike Jinyang, and catch them unawares—this seems the superior strategy.
translations.idiomatic: According to my plan, we should advance through Fen and Lu, directly strike at Jinyang, and catch them unprepared—this seems the superior strategy.

sentences.zh: 」周主皆不從。

translations.literal: " The Zhou ruler did not follow any of them.
translations.idiomatic: " The Zhou emperor did not follow any of these proposals.

sentences.zh: 宏，泉之弟也。

translations.literal: Hong was Quan's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Hong was the younger brother of Bao Quan.

sentences.zh: 壬午，周主帥眾六萬，直指河陰。

translations.literal: On renwu, the Zhou ruler led sixty thousand troops straight at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, the Zhou emperor led sixty thousand troops straight toward Heyin.

sentences.zh: 楊素請帥其父麾下先驅，周主許之。

translations.literal: Yang Su requested to command his father's troops as vanguard; the Zhou ruler granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su requested to lead his father's troops as vanguard; the Zhou emperor permitted it.

sentences.zh: 八月，癸卯，周遣使來聘。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on guimao, Zhou sent envoys on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on guimao, Zhou sent envoys on a friendly mission.

sentences.zh: 周師入齊境，禁伐樹踐稼，犯者皆斬。

translations.literal: When Zhou troops entered Qi territory, they forbade cutting trees or trampling crops; violators were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou armies entered Qi territory, they forbade cutting trees or trampling crops; violators were all executed.

sentences.zh: 丁未，周主攻河陰大城，拔之。

translations.literal: On dingwei, the Zhou ruler attacked the great city of Heyin and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, the Zhou emperor attacked the great city of Heyin and captured it.

sentences.zh: 齊王憲拔武濟；

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Xian captured Wuji;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Qi captured Wuji;

sentences.zh: 進圍洛口，拔東、西二城，縱火焚浮橋，橋絕。

translations.literal: advancing to besiege Luokou, he captured the eastern and western cities, set fire and burned the pontoon bridge, and the bridge was severed.
translations.idiomatic: advancing to besiege Luokou, he captured the eastern and western cities, set fire to the pontoon bridge, and severed the bridge.

sentences.zh: 齊永橋大都督太安傅伏，自永橋夜入中水單城。

translations.literal: Fu Fu of Tai'an, Northern Qi Grand Governor of Yongqiao, by night from Yongqiao entered Zhongshuidan city.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Fu of Tai'an, Grand Governor of Yongqiao in Qi, entered Zhongshuidan city by night from Yongqiao.

sentences.zh: 周人既克南城，圍中水單，二旬不下。

translations.literal: After the Zhou men had captured the southern city, they besieged Zhongshuidan for twenty days without taking it.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhou forces had taken the southern city, they besieged Zhongshuidan for twenty days without capturing it.

sentences.zh: 洛州刺史獨孤永業守金墉，周主自攻之，不克。

translations.literal: Luozhou Prefect Dugu Yongye defended Jinyong; the Zhou ruler personally attacked it but could not capture it.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Yongye, Prefect of Luozhou, defended Jinyong; the Zhou emperor personally attacked it but could not take it.

sentences.zh: 永業通夜辦馬槽二千，周人聞之，以為大軍且至而憚之。

translations.literal: Yongye worked through the night preparing two thousand horse troughs; when the Zhou men heard of it, they thought a great army was about to arrive and feared it.
translations.idiomatic: Yongye worked through the night preparing two thousand horse troughs; when the Zhou forces heard of this, they thought a large army was about to arrive and were intimidated.

sentences.zh: 九月，齊右丞高阿那肱自晉陽將兵拒周師。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Northern Qi Right Chancellor Gao Anaguhu led troops from Jinyang to resist the Zhou armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Gao Anagong, Right Chancellor of Qi, led troops from Jinyang to resist the Zhou armies.

sentences.zh: 至河陽，會周主有疾，辛酉夜，引兵還。

translations.literal: Reaching Heyang, it happened that the Zhou ruler was ill; on the night of xinyou he withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Heyang, the Zhou emperor fell ill; on the night of xinyou he withdrew his troops.

sentences.zh: 水軍焚其舟艦。

translations.literal: The naval forces burned their ships.
translations.idiomatic: The naval forces burned their ships.

sentences.zh: 傅伏謂行台乞伏貴和曰：「周師疲弊，願得精騎二千追擊之，可破也。

translations.literal: Fu Fu said to Xingtai Qifu Guihe: "The Zhou armies are worn and exhausted; if I am given two thousand elite cavalry to pursue them, they can be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Fu said to Xingtai Qifu Guihe, "The Zhou armies are exhausted; if I am granted two thousand elite cavalry to pursue them, they can be defeated.

sentences.zh: 」貴和不許。

translations.literal: " Guihe did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: " Guihe did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 齊王憲、於翼、李穆，所向克捷，降拔三十餘城，皆棄而不守。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Xian, Yu Yi, and Li Mu met with success wherever they went, capturing or receiving the surrender of more than thirty cities, all of which they abandoned without holding.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Qi, Yu Yi, and Li Mu met with success wherever they went, capturing or receiving the surrender of more than thirty cities, all of which they abandoned without garrisoning.

sentences.zh: 唯以王藥城要害，令儀同三司韓正守之，正尋以城降齊。

translations.literal: Only at the strategic Wangyao city did they appoint Han Zheng, Senior General of the Third Rank, to guard it; Zheng soon surrendered the city to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Only for the strategic Wangyao city did they appoint Han Zheng, Senior General of the Third Rank, to hold it; Zheng soon surrendered the city to Qi.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，周主還長安。

translations.literal: On wuyin, the Zhou ruler returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, the Zhou emperor returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，齊以趙彥深為司徒，斛阿列羅為司空。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Qi appointed Zhao Yanshen as Minister over the Masses and Hu Alieluo as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Qi appointed Zhao Yanshen as Minister over the Masses and Hu Alieluo as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 閏月，車騎大將軍吳明徹將兵擊齊彭城；

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, General of Chariots and Cavalry Wu Mingche led troops to attack Pengcheng in Qi;
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, General of Chariots and Cavalry Wu Mingche led troops to attack Pengcheng in Qi;

sentences.zh: 壬辰，敗齊兵數萬於呂梁。

translations.literal: on renchen he defeated tens of thousands of Qi troops at Lüliang.
translations.idiomatic: on renchen he defeated tens of thousands of Qi troops at Lüliang.

sentences.zh: 甲午，周主如同州。

translations.literal: On jiawu, the Zhou ruler went to Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, the Zhou emperor went to Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己巳，立皇子叔齊為新蔡王，叔文為晉熙王。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jisi, Prince Shuji was enfeoffed as Prince of Xincai and Prince Shuwén was enfeoffed as Prince of Jinxi.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jisi, the princes Shuji and Shuwén were enfeoffed as Prince of Xincai and Prince of Jinxi respectively.

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛亥朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the xinhai new moon, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the xinhai new moon, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以王瑒為尚書左僕射，太子詹事吳郡陸繕為右僕射。

translations.literal: On renxu, Wang Chang was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Lu Shan of Wu Commandery, Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, was appointed Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Wang Chang was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Lu Shan of Wu Commandery, Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, was appointed Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 庚午，周主還長安。

translations.literal: On gengwu, the Zhou ruler returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, the Zhou emperor returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 高宗宣皇帝中之上太建八年（丙申，公元五七六年） 。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan of Chen, middle reign, upper part: Taikjian year 8 (bingshen, AD 576).
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan of Chen, middle reign, upper part: Taikjian year 8 (bingshen, AD 576).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸未，周主如同州；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on guiwei, the Zhou ruler went to Tong Province;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on guiwei, the Zhou emperor went to Tong Province;

sentences.zh: 辛卯，如河東涑川；

translations.literal: on xinmao, he went to Hedong Suichuan;
translations.idiomatic: on xinmao, he went to Hedong Suichuan;

sentences.zh: 甲午，復還同州。

translations.literal: on jiawu, he again returned to Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: on jiawu, he again returned to Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，齊大赦。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Northern Qi proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Northern Qi proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，齊主還鄴。

translations.literal: On yimao, the Qi ruler returned to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, the Northern Qi emperor returned to Ye.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛酉，周主命太子巡撫西土，因伐吐谷渾，上開府儀同大將軍王軌、宮正宇文孝伯從行。

translations.literal: In the second month, on xinyou, the Zhou ruler ordered the crown prince to inspect the western regions and meanwhile attack Tuyuhun; Senior General of the Third Rank Wang Gui and Palace Director Yuwen Xiaobo accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinyou, the Zhou emperor ordered the crown prince to inspect the western regions and meanwhile attack Tuyuhun; Senior General of the Third Rank Wang Gui and Palace Director Yuwen Xiaobo accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 軍中節度，皆委二人，太子仰成而已。

translations.literal: All military command in the army was entrusted to the two of them; the crown prince merely accepted what was accomplished for him.
translations.idiomatic: All military command in the army was entrusted to the two of them; the crown prince merely accepted what was accomplished for him.

sentences.zh: 齊括雜戶未嫁者悉集，有隱匿者，家長坐死。

translations.literal: Northern Qi gathered all unmarried women among the miscellaneous households; those who concealed anyone—the head of household was punished by death.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi gathered all unmarried women among the miscellaneous households; those who concealed anyone—the head of household was punished by death.

sentences.zh: 壬申，以開府儀同三司吳明徹為司空。

translations.literal: On renshen, Wu Mingche, Senior General of the Third Rank, was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Wu Mingche, Senior General of the Third Rank, was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬寅，周主還長安；

translations.literal: In the third month, on renyin, the Zhou ruler returned to Chang'an;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on renyin, the Zhou emperor returned to Chang'an;

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙卯，復如同州。

translations.literal: in summer, the fourth month, on yimao, he again went to Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: in summer, the fourth month, on yimao, he again went to Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 己未，上享太廟。

translations.literal: On jiwei, the emperor offered sacrifice at the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, the Chen emperor offered sacrifice at the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射王瑒。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Wang Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Wang Chang.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬辰，周主還長安。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on renchen, the Zhou ruler returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on renchen, the Zhou emperor returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 六月，戊申朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the wushen new moon, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the wushen new moon, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，周主享太廟。

translations.literal: On xinhai, the Zhou ruler offered sacrifice at the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, the Zhou emperor offered sacrifice at the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 初，太子叔寶欲以左戶部尚書江總為詹事，令管記陸瑜言於吏部尚書孔奐。

translations.literal: Previously, Crown Prince Shubao wished to appoint Jiang Zong, Director of the Left Ministry of Household Affairs, as Grand Tutor, and had Recorder Lu Yu speak to Kong Huan, Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, Crown Prince Shubao wished to appoint Jiang Zong, Director of the Left Ministry of Household Affairs, as Grand Tutor, and had Recorder Lu Yu speak to Kong Huan, Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 奐謂瑜曰：「江有潘、陸之華而無園、綺之實，輔弼儲宮，竊有所難。

translations.literal: Huan said to Yu: "Jiang has the brilliance of Pan and Lu but lacks the solid substance of Dong and Qi; to assist and support the heir apparent—privately I find it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Huan said to Yu, "Jiang has the literary brilliance of Pan Yue and Lu Ji but lacks the solid substance of Dong Zhongshu and Qi Li Ji; to assist and support the heir apparent, I privately find it difficult.

sentences.zh: 」太子深以為恨，自言於帝。

translations.literal: " The crown prince deeply resented this and spoke of it himself to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince deeply resented this and spoke of it himself to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝將許之，奐奏曰：「江總，文華之士。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to grant it; Huan submitted: "Jiang Zong is a man of literary brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to grant it; Kong Huan submitted, "Jiang Zong is a man of literary brilliance.

sentences.zh: 今皇太子文華不少，豈藉於總！

translations.literal: Now the crown prince's literary brilliance is not lacking—why rely on Zong!
translations.idiomatic: Now the crown prince's literary brilliance is not lacking—why rely on Zong!

sentences.zh: 如臣愚見，願選敦重之才，以居輔導之職。

translations.literal: According to my humble view, I wish to select a man of solid weight to hold the post of guiding and assisting.
translations.idiomatic: According to my humble view, I wish to select a man of solid weight to hold the post of guiding and assisting.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「即如卿言，誰當居此？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "If it is as you say, who should hold this?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "If it is as you say, who should hold this post?

sentences.zh: 」奐曰：「都官尚書王廓，世有懿德，識性敦敏，可以居之。

translations.literal: " Huan said: "Wang Kuo, Director of the Palace Law Enforcement, for generations has possessed virtuous conduct; in knowledge and character he is solid and quick—he can hold it.
translations.idiomatic: " Kong Huan said, "Wang Kuo, Director of the Palace Law Enforcement, for generations has possessed virtuous conduct; in knowledge and character he is solid and quick—he can hold it.

sentences.zh: 」太子時在側，乃曰：「廓，王泰之子，不宜為太子詹事。

translations.literal: " The crown prince was then at his side and said: "Kuo is the son of Wang Tai; unsuitable to be Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince, who was then at his side, said, "Kuo is the son of Wang Tai—he is unsuitable to serve as Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 」奐曰：「宋朝范曄即范泰之子，亦為太子詹事，前代不疑。

translations.literal: " Huan said: "In the Song dynasty Fan Ye was the son of Fan Tai, and also served as Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince; former generations did not doubt this.
translations.idiomatic: " Kong Huan said, "In the Song dynasty Fan Ye was the son of Fan Tai and also served as Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince—former generations raised no objection.

sentences.zh: 」太子固爭之，帝卒以總為詹事。

translations.literal: " The crown prince firmly contested this; the emperor ultimately made Zong Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince firmly contested this, but the Chen emperor ultimately appointed Zong as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 總，學之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Zong was the great-grandson of Xue Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zong was the great-grandson of Xue Zhi.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以尚書右僕射陸繕為左僕射。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Lu Shan, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was made Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Lu Shan, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was made Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 帝欲以孔奐代繕，詔已出，太子沮之而止；

translations.literal: The emperor wished to replace Shan with Kong Huan; the edict had already been issued, but the crown prince dissuaded him and he stopped;
translations.idiomatic: The Chen emperor wished to replace Shan with Kong Huan; the edict had already been issued, but the crown prince dissuaded him and he stopped;

sentences.zh: 更以晉陵太守王克為右僕射。

translations.literal: Wang Ke, Prefect of Jinling, was instead made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ke, Prefect of Jinling, was instead made Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 頃之，總與太子為長夜之飲，養良娣陳氏為女；

translations.literal: Before long, Zong and the crown prince held all-night drinking sessions, and Zong adopted a secondary consort, the Lady Chen, as his daughter;
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Zong and the crown prince held all-night drinking sessions, and Zong adopted a secondary consort, the Lady Chen, as his daughter;

sentences.zh: 太子亟微行，游總家。

translations.literal: the crown prince repeatedly made secret outings to visit Zong's home.
translations.idiomatic: the crown prince repeatedly made secret outings to visit Zong's home.

sentences.zh: 上怒，免總官。

translations.literal: The emperor was angered and dismissed Zong from office.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen emperor was angered and dismissed Zong from office.

sentences.zh: 周利州刺史紀王康，驕矜無度，繕修戎器，陰有異謀。

translations.literal: Prince Kang of Ji, Governor of Lizhou in Zhou, was arrogant and unrestrained beyond measure; he repaired weapons of war and secretly harbored treasonous designs.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kang of Ji, Governor of Lizhou in Zhou, was arrogant and unrestrained beyond measure; he repaired weapons of war and secretly harbored treasonous designs.

sentences.zh: 司錄裴融諫止之，康殺融。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Pei Rong remonstrated and tried to stop him; Kang killed Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Pei Rong remonstrated and tried to stop him; Kang killed Rong.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，賜康死。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Kang was ordered to take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Kang was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，周主如雲陽。

translations.literal: On dingsi, the Zhou ruler went to Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, the Zhou emperor went to Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 庚申，齊宜陽王趙彥深卒。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Zhao Yanshen, Prince of Yiyang of Qi, died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Zhao Yanshen, Prince of Yiyang of Qi, died.

sentences.zh: 彥深歷事累朝，常參機近，以溫謹著稱。

translations.literal: Yanshen had served through successive reigns, regularly taking part in confidential affairs close to the throne, and was renowned for his warmth and prudence.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshen had served through successive reigns, regularly taking part in confidential affairs close to the throne, and was renowned for his warmth and prudence.

sentences.zh: 既卒，朝貴典機密者，唯侍中、開府儀同三司斛律孝卿一人而已，其餘皆嬖倖也。

translations.literal: After he died, among the court nobility entrusted with confidential affairs there remained only one man—Hulü Xiaoqing, Palace Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Equivalent Rank to the Three Excellencies; all the rest were intimate favorites.
translations.idiomatic: After he died, among the court nobility entrusted with confidential affairs there remained only one man—Hulü Xiaoqing, Palace Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Equivalent Rank to the Three Excellencies; all the rest were intimate favorites.

sentences.zh: 孝卿，羌舉之子，比於餘人，差不貪穢。

translations.literal: Xiaoqing was the son of Qiang Ju; compared with the others, he was somewhat less greedy and corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoqing was the son of Qiang Ju; compared with the others, he was somewhat less greedy and corrupt.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，乙卯，周主還長安。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on yimao, the Zhou ruler returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on yimao, the Zhou emperor returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 周太子伐吐谷渾，至伏俟城而還。

translations.literal: The Zhou crown prince marched against Tuyuhun, reached Fuyucheng, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou crown prince marched against Tuyuhun, reached Fuyucheng, and returned.

sentences.zh: 宮尹鄭譯、王端等皆有寵於太子。

translations.literal: Palace Secretary Zheng Yi, Wang Duan, and others all enjoyed the crown prince's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretary Zheng Yi, Wang Duan, and others all enjoyed the crown prince's favor.

sentences.zh: 太子在軍中多失德，譯等皆預焉。

translations.literal: The crown prince committed many offenses while in the army, and Yi and the others all took part in them.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince committed many offenses while in the army, and Yi and the others all took part in them.

sentences.zh: 軍還，王軌等言之於周主。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Wang Gui and the others reported this to the Zhou ruler.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, Wang Gui and the others reported this to the Zhou emperor.

sentences.zh: 周主怒，杖太子及譯等，仍除譯等名，宮臣親幸者鹹被譴。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler was enraged; he beat the crown prince and Yi and the others, removed Yi and the others from the register, and all palace attendants close to the crown prince were rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor was enraged; he beat the crown prince and Yi and the others, removed Yi and the others from the register, and all palace attendants close to the crown prince were rebuked.

sentences.zh: 太子復召譯，戲狎如初。

translations.literal: The crown prince again summoned Yi and was as playful and familiar with him as before.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince again summoned Yi and was as playful and familiar with him as before.

sentences.zh: 譯因曰：「殿下何時可得據天下？

translations.literal: Yi then said: "Your Highness, when will you be able to seize the empire?
translations.idiomatic: Yi then said, "Your Highness, when will you be able to seize the empire?

sentences.zh: 」太子悅，益暱之。

translations.literal: " The crown prince was pleased and grew even more intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince was pleased and grew even more intimate with him.

sentences.zh: 譯，儼之兄孫也。

translations.literal: Yi was the elder brother's grandson of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was the grandson of Yan's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 周主遇太子甚嚴，每朝見，進止與群臣無異，雖隆寒盛暑，不得休息；

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler treated the crown prince very sternly; whenever he attended audience, his comings and goings were no different from those of the officials—even in bitter cold or blazing heat, he was given no respite;
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor treated the crown prince very sternly; whenever he attended audience, his comings and goings were no different from those of the officials—even in bitter cold or blazing heat, he was given no respite;

sentences.zh: 以其耆酒，禁酒不得至東宮；

translations.literal: because he was fond of wine, he was forbidden wine and could not go to the Eastern Palace;
translations.idiomatic: because he was fond of wine, he was forbidden wine and could not go to the Eastern Palace;

sentences.zh: 有過，輒加捶撻。

translations.literal: whenever he committed an offense, he was immediately beaten.
translations.idiomatic: whenever he committed an offense, he was immediately beaten.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂之曰：「古來太子被廢者幾人？

translations.literal: He once said to him: "Throughout history, how many crown princes have been deposed?
translations.idiomatic: He once said to him, "Throughout history, how many crown princes have been deposed?

sentences.zh: 余兒豈不堪立邪！

translations.literal: Is my son truly unfit to be established!
translations.idiomatic: Is my son truly unfit to be established!

sentences.zh: 」乃敕東宮官屬錄太子言語動作，每月奏聞。

translations.literal: " He then ordered the Eastern Palace officials to record the crown prince's words, deeds, and movements, and report them monthly.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered the Eastern Palace officials to record the crown prince's words, deeds, and movements, and report them monthly.

sentences.zh: 太子畏帝威嚴，矯情修飾，由是過惡不上聞。

translations.literal: The crown prince feared the emperor's awe-inspiring sternness, feigned virtue and cultivated appearances, and thus his faults and misdeeds went unreported.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince feared the Zhou emperor's awe-inspiring sternness, feigned virtue and cultivated appearances, and thus his faults and misdeeds went unreported.

sentences.zh: 王軌嘗與小內史賀若弼言：「太子必不克負荷。

translations.literal: Wang Gui once said to Junior Palace Secretary Heluo Bi: "The crown prince will certainly be unable to bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui once said to Junior Palace Secretary Heluo Bi, "The crown prince will certainly be unable to bear the burden.

sentences.zh: 」弼深以為然，勸軌陳之。

translations.literal: " Bi deeply agreed and urged Gui to present this to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: " Bi deeply agreed and urged Gui to present this to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 軌後因侍坐，言於帝曰：「皇太子仁孝無聞，恐不了陛下家事。

translations.literal: Later, while attending the emperor, Gui said to him: "The crown prince has no reputation for benevolence or filial piety; I fear he will not be able to manage Your Majesty's household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while attending the Zhou emperor, Gui said to him, "The crown prince has no reputation for benevolence or filial piety; I fear he will not be able to manage Your Majesty's household affairs.

sentences.zh: 愚臣短暗，不足可信。

translations.literal: This foolish minister is shallow and dull—not to be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: This foolish minister is shallow and dull—not to be trusted.

sentences.zh: 陛下恆以賀若弼有文武奇才，亦常以此為憂。

translations.literal: Your Majesty always considers Heluo Bi to possess extraordinary talent in both civil and military affairs, and is often troubled on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty always considers Heluo Bi to possess extraordinary talent in both civil and military affairs, and is often troubled on that account.

sentences.zh: 」帝以問弼，對曰：「皇太子養德春宮，未聞有過。

translations.literal: " The emperor questioned Bi about this; he replied: "The crown prince is cultivating virtue in the Eastern Palace, and none of his faults have been heard of.
translations.idiomatic: " The Zhou emperor questioned Bi about this; he replied, "The crown prince is cultivating virtue in the Eastern Palace, and none of his faults have been heard of.

sentences.zh: 」既退，軌讓弼曰：「平生言論，無所不道，今者對揚，何得乃爾反覆？

translations.literal: " After they withdrew, Gui reproached Bi: "In our talks throughout our lives we have discussed everything—why, when answering before the throne today, have you reversed yourself so?
translations.idiomatic: " After they withdrew, Gui reproached Bi, "In our talks throughout our lives we have discussed everything—why, when answering before the throne today, have you reversed yourself so?

sentences.zh: 」弼曰：「此公之過也。

translations.literal: " Bi said: "That was Your Excellency's fault.
translations.idiomatic: " Bi said, "That was Your Excellency's fault.

sentences.zh: 太子，國之儲副，豈易發言！

translations.literal: The crown prince is the heir of the state—how easily can one speak about him!
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is the heir of the state—how easily can one speak about him!

sentences.zh: 事有蹉跌，便至滅族。

translations.literal: If matters go awry, it leads straight to the extinction of one's clan.
translations.idiomatic: If matters go awry, it leads straight to the extinction of one's clan.

sentences.zh: 本謂公密陳臧否。

translations.literal: I thought Your Excellency would privately present your praise or blame.
translations.idiomatic: I thought Your Excellency would privately present your praise or blame.

sentences.zh: 何得遂至昌言！

translations.literal: How could you bring it forth to open declaration!
translations.idiomatic: How could you bring it forth to open declaration!

sentences.zh: 」軌默然久之，乃曰：「吾專心國家，遂不存私計。

translations.literal: " Gui was silent for a long time, then said: "I devote myself single-mindedly to the state and have no concern for private calculation.
translations.idiomatic: " Gui was silent for a long time, then said, "I devote myself single-mindedly to the state and have no concern for private calculation.

sentences.zh: 向者對眾，良實非宜。

translations.literal: Speaking before the assembly as I did was truly inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking before the assembly as I did was truly inappropriate.

sentences.zh: 後軌因內宴上壽，捋帝須曰：「可愛好老公，但恨後嗣弱耳。

translations.literal: Later, at an inner-court banquet where he was offering birthday felicitations, Gui stroked the emperor's beard and said: "What a dear old lord—but how I regret that his successor is weak!
translations.idiomatic: Later, at an inner-court banquet where he was offering birthday felicitations, Gui stroked the Zhou emperor's beard and said, "What a dear old lord—but how I regret that his successor is weak!

sentences.zh: 」先是，帝問右宮伯宇文孝伯曰：「吾兒比來何如？

translations.literal: " Earlier, the emperor had asked Yuwen Xiaobo, Right Director of the Eastern Palace: "How has my son been lately?
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier, the Zhou emperor had asked Yuwen Xiaobo, Right Director of the Eastern Palace, "How has my son been lately?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「太子比懼天威，更無過失。

translations.literal: " He replied: "The crown prince, fearing Heaven's majesty, has had no further misdeeds.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "The crown prince, fearing Heaven's majesty, has had no further misdeeds.

sentences.zh: 」罷酒，帝責孝伯曰：「公常語我云：『太子無過。

translations.literal: " When the drinking ended, the emperor reproached Xiaobo: "You have often told me, 'The crown prince has no faults.
translations.idiomatic: " When the drinking ended, the Zhou emperor reproached Xiaobo, "You have often told me, 'The crown prince has no faults.

sentences.zh: 』今軌有此言，公為誑矣。

translations.literal: ' Yet now Gui has said this—you have deceived me.
translations.idiomatic: ' Yet now Gui has said this—you have deceived me.

sentences.zh: 」孝伯再拜曰：「臣聞父子之際，人所難言。

translations.literal: " Xiaobo bowed twice and said: "Your subject has heard that between father and son, it is what men find hardest to speak of.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaobo bowed twice and said, "Your subject has heard that between father and son, it is what men find hardest to speak of.

sentences.zh: 臣知陛下不能割慈忍愛，遂爾結舌。

translations.literal: Your subject knew Your Majesty could not cut off affection and endure harsh love, and so held his tongue.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject knew Your Majesty could not cut off affection and endure harsh love, and so held his tongue.

sentences.zh: 」帝知其意，默然久之，乃曰：「朕已委公矣，公其勉之。

translations.literal: " The emperor understood his meaning, was silent a long while, then said: "I have already entrusted this to you—please exert yourself.
translations.idiomatic: " The Zhou emperor understood his meaning, was silent a long while, then said, "I have already entrusted this to you—please exert yourself.

sentences.zh: 王軌驟言於帝曰：「皇太子非社稷主。

translations.literal: Wang Gui suddenly said to the emperor: "The crown prince is no fit master for the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui suddenly said to the Zhou emperor, "The crown prince is no fit master for the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 普六茹堅貌有反相。

translations.literal: Yang Jian of Puliuru has the look of a rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian of Puliuru has the look of a rebel.

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅，曰：「必天命有在，將若之何！

translations.literal: " The emperor was displeased and said: "If destiny must rest with someone, what can be done!
translations.idiomatic: " The Zhou emperor was displeased and said, "If destiny must rest with someone, what can be done!

sentences.zh: 」楊堅聞之，甚懼，深自晦匿。

translations.literal: " When Yang Jian heard of this, he was greatly afraid and deeply concealed himself.
translations.idiomatic: " When Yang Jian heard of this, he was greatly afraid and deeply concealed himself.

sentences.zh: 帝深以軌等言為然，但漢王贊次長，又不才，余子皆幼，故得不廢。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply believed what Gui and the others had said was true, but Prince of Han Zan was next eldest and also lacking in talent, and the remaining sons were all young—thus the crown prince was not deposed.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor deeply believed what Gui and the others had said was true, but Prince Zan of Han was next eldest and also lacking in talent, and the remaining sons were all young—thus the crown prince was not deposed.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以司空吳明徹為南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Wu Mingche, Minister of Works, was made Inspector of Southern Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Wu Mingche, Minister of Works, was made Inspector of Southern Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 齊主如晉陽。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler went to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi emperor went to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 營邯鄲宮。

translations.literal: He built the Handan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Handan Palace.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊戌，以皇子叔彪為淮南王。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on wuxu, the emperor's son Shubiao was made Prince of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on wuxu, the Chen emperor's son Shubiao was made Prince of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 周主謂群臣曰：「朕去歲屬有疾疹，遂不得克平逋寇。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler said to the assembled ministers: "Last year I happened to suffer from illness, and so was unable to subdue the fugitive enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor said to the assembled ministers, "Last year I happened to suffer from illness, and so was unable to subdue the fugitive enemy.

sentences.zh: 前入齊境，備見其情，彼之行師，殆同兒戲。

translations.literal: When I previously entered Qi territory, I saw their condition in full—their conduct of war is almost child's play.
translations.idiomatic: When I previously entered Qi territory, I saw their condition in full—their conduct of war is almost child's play.

sentences.zh: 況其朝廷昏亂，政由群小；

translations.literal: Moreover, their court is muddled and corrupt, with government in the hands of petty men;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, their court is muddled and corrupt, with government in the hands of petty men;

sentences.zh: 百姓嗷然，朝不謀夕。

translations.literal: the people cry out in distress, with neither morning nor evening secure.
translations.idiomatic: the people cry out in distress, with neither morning nor evening secure.

sentences.zh: 天與不取，恐貽後悔。

translations.literal: Heaven grants yet we do not take—fear lest we leave regret behind.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven grants yet we do not take—fear lest we leave regret behind.

sentences.zh: 前出河外，直為拊背，未扼其喉。

translations.literal: Previously we went beyond the river—it was merely patting the back, not grasping the throat.
translations.idiomatic: Previously we went beyond the river—it was merely patting the back, not grasping the throat.

sentences.zh: 晉州本高歡所起之地，鎮攝要重，今往攻之，彼必來援；

translations.literal: Jin Province was originally where Gao Huan rose to power; it is a key garrison of supreme importance. If we attack it now, they will surely come to its aid;
translations.idiomatic: Jin Province was originally where Gao Huan rose to power; it is a key garrison of supreme importance. If we attack it now, they will surely come to its aid;

sentences.zh: 吾嚴軍以待，擊之必克。

translations.literal: We shall hold our army in strict readiness and await them—we will defeat them for certain.
translations.idiomatic: We shall hold our army in strict readiness and await them—we will defeat them for certain.

sentences.zh: 然後乘破竹之勢，鼓行而東，足以窮其巢穴，混同文軌。

translations.literal: Then, riding the momentum of splitting bamboo, we shall march east with drums beating—enough to exhaust their lair and unite culture and cart-tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Then, riding the momentum of splitting bamboo, we shall march east with drums beating—enough to exhaust their lair and unite culture and cart-tracks.

sentences.zh: 」諸將多不願行。

translations.literal: " Many of the generals were unwilling to go.
translations.idiomatic: " Many of the generals were unwilling to go.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「機不可失。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The opportunity must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor said, "The opportunity must not be lost.

sentences.zh: 有沮吾軍者，當以軍法裁之！

translations.literal: Whoever discourages our army shall be judged by military law!
translations.idiomatic: Whoever discourages our army shall be judged by military law!

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己酉，周主自將伐齊，以越王盛、杞公亮、隨公楊堅為右三軍，譙王儉、大將軍竇泰、廣化公丘崇為左三軍，齊王憲、陳王純為前軍。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiyou, the Zhou ruler personally led a campaign against Qi, appointing Prince Sheng of Yue, Duke Liang of Qi, and Duke Yang Jian of Sui as the Right Three Armies; Prince Jian of Qiao, Grand General Dou Tai, and Duke Qiu Chong of Guanghua as the Left Three Armies; and Prince Xian of Qi and Prince Chun of Chen as the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiyou, the Zhou emperor personally led a campaign against Qi, appointing Prince Sheng of Yue, Duke Liang of Qi, and Duke Yang Jian of Sui as the Right Three Armies; Prince Jian of Qiao, Grand General Dou Tai, and Duke Qiu Chong of Guanghua as the Left Three Armies; and Prince Xian of Qi and Prince Chun of Chen as the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 亮，導之子也。

translations.literal: Liang was the son of Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was the son of Dao.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，齊主獵於祁連池；

translations.literal: On bingchen, the Qi ruler hunted at Qilian Pool;
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, the Northern Qi emperor hunted at Qilian Pool;

sentences.zh: 癸亥，還晉陽。

translations.literal: On guihai, he returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, he returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 先是，晉州行台左丞張延雋公直勤敏，儲偫有備，百姓安業。

translations.literal: Previously, Zhang Yanjuan, Left Assistant Director of the Jin Province Executive, was upright, diligent, and quick-witted; stores were stocked and defenses ready, and the people pursued their livelihoods in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, Zhang Yanjuan, Left Assistant Director of the Jin Province Executive, was upright, diligent, and quick-witted; provisions were stocked and defenses ready, and the people lived and worked in peace.

sentences.zh: 疆場無虞。

translations.literal: The frontier was untroubled.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier was untroubled.

sentences.zh: 諸嬖倖惡而代之，由是公私煩擾。

translations.literal: The various favorites resented him and had him replaced, whereupon both public and private affairs fell into turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: The various favorites resented him and had him replaced, whereupon both public and private affairs fell into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 周主至晉州，軍於汾曲，遣齊王憲將精騎二萬守雀鼠谷，陳王純步騎二萬守千里徑，鄭公達奚震步騎一萬守統軍川，大將軍韓明步騎五千守齊子嶺，焉氏公尹升步騎五千守鼓鐘鎮，涼城公辛韶步騎五千守蒲津關，趙王招步騎一萬自華谷攻齊汾州諸城，柱國宇文盛步騎一萬守汾水關。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler arrived at Jin Province and encamped at Fen Bend. He sent Prince Xian of Qi to lead twenty thousand elite horsemen to guard Que-shu Valley; Prince Chun of Chen with twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to guard Qianli Pass; Duke Zhen of Zheng with ten thousand infantry and cavalry to guard Tongjun River; Grand General Han Ming with five thousand infantry and cavalry to guard Qizi Ridge; Duke Sheng of the Yan clan with five thousand infantry and cavalry to guard Guchong Fort; Duke Shao of Liangcheng with five thousand infantry and cavalry to guard Pujin Pass; Prince Zhao with ten thousand infantry and cavalry to attack the various cities of Fen Province in Qi from Huagu; and Chief Minister Yuwen Sheng with ten thousand infantry and cavalry to guard Fenshui Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor arrived at Jin Province and encamped at Fen Bend. He sent Prince Xian of Qi to lead twenty thousand elite horsemen to guard Que-shu Valley; Prince Chun of Chen with twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to guard Qianli Pass; Duke Zhen of Zheng with ten thousand infantry and cavalry to guard Tongjun River; Grand General Han Ming with five thousand infantry and cavalry to guard Qizi Ridge; Duke Sheng of the Yan clan with five thousand infantry and cavalry to guard Guchong Fort; Duke Shao of Liangcheng with five thousand infantry and cavalry to guard Pujin Pass; Prince Zhao with ten thousand infantry and cavalry to attack the various cities of Fen Province in Qi from Huagu; and Chief Minister Yuwen Sheng with ten thousand infantry and cavalry to guard Fenshui Pass.

sentences.zh: 遣內史王誼監諸軍攻平陽城。

translations.literal: He sent Palace Secretary Wang Yi to supervise the various armies in the assault on Pingyang city.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Palace Secretary Wang Yi to supervise the various armies in the assault on Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 齊行台僕射海昌王尉相貴嬰城拒守。

translations.literal: Wei Xianggui, Prince of Haichang and Vice Director of the Qi Executive, closed the city gates and held out in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xianggui, Prince of Haichang and Vice Director of the Northern Qi Executive, closed the city gates and held out in defense.

sentences.zh: 相貴，相願之兄也。

translations.literal: Xianggui was the elder brother of Xiangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggui was the elder brother of Xiangyuan.

sentences.zh: 甲子，齊集兵晉祠。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Qi assembled troops at Jin Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, the Qi forces assembled at Jin Shrine.

sentences.zh: 庚午，齊主自晉陽帥諸軍趣晉州。

translations.literal: On gengwu, the Qi ruler personally led the various armies from Jinyang toward Jin Province.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, the Northern Qi emperor personally led the various armies from Jinyang toward Jin Province.

sentences.zh: 周主日自汾曲至城下督戰，城中窘急。

translations.literal: Day after day the Zhou ruler came from Fen Bend to beneath the city walls to supervise the fighting, and within the city distress grew acute.
translations.idiomatic: Day after day the Zhou emperor came from Fen Bend to beneath the city walls to direct the fighting, while distress within the city grew acute.

sentences.zh: 庚午，行台左丞侯子欽出降於周。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Hou Ziqin, Left Assistant Director of the Executive, went out and surrendered to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Hou Ziqin, Left Assistant Director of the Executive, went out and surrendered to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 壬申，晉州刺史崔景嵩守北城，夜，遣使請降於周，王軌帥眾應之。

translations.literal: On renshen, Cui Jingsong, Governor of Jin Province, held the north city. At night he sent envoys to request surrender to Zhou, and Wang Gui led troops to respond.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Cui Jingsong, Governor of Jin Province, held the north city. That night he sent envoys to request surrender to Zhou, and Wang Gui led troops to respond.

sentences.zh: 未明，周將北海段文振，杖槊與數十人先登，與景嵩同至尉相貴所，拔佩刀劫之。

translations.literal: Before dawn, the Zhou general Duan Wenzhen of Beihai, spear in hand, climbed up first with several dozen men. He and Jingsong went together to Wei Xianggui's quarters and drew his belt knife to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn, the Zhou general Duan Wenzhen of Beihai, spear in hand, climbed up first with several dozen men. He and Jingsong went together to Wei Xianggui's quarters, where he drew his belt knife and seized him.

sentences.zh: 城上鼓噪，齊兵大潰，遂克晉州，虜相貴及甲士八千人。

translations.literal: Drums and shouts rose on the walls; the Qi troops broke in great rout. They thereupon captured Jin Province and took Xianggui and eight thousand armored soldiers prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Drums and shouts rose on the walls, and the Qi troops broke in great rout. Zhou forces thereupon captured Jin Province and took Xianggui and eight thousand armored soldiers prisoner.

sentences.zh: 齊主方與馮淑妃獵於天池，晉州告急者，自旦至午，驛馬三至。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler was just then hunting at Tianchi with Lady Feng the Pure Consort. Urgent reports from Jin Province arrived—from dawn until noon, courier horses came three times.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi emperor was just then hunting at Tianchi with Lady Feng the Pure Consort. Urgent reports from Jin Province arrived—from dawn until noon, courier horses came three times.

sentences.zh: 右丞相高阿那肱曰：「大家正為樂，邊鄙小小交兵，乃是常事，何急奏聞！

translations.literal: Right Chancellor Gao Anahoug said: "His Majesty is at his pleasure. Small clashes on the frontier are an ordinary matter—why report them in such haste!
translations.idiomatic: Right Chancellor Gao Anahoug said, "His Majesty is enjoying himself. Minor skirmishes on the frontier are an ordinary matter—why report them in such haste!

sentences.zh: 」至暮，使更至，云「平陽已陷」，乃奏之。

translations.literal: " By evening another messenger arrived saying, "Pingyang has already fallen," and only then did he report it.
translations.idiomatic: " By evening another messenger arrived saying, "Pingyang has already fallen," and only then did he report it.

sentences.zh: 齊主將還，淑妃請更殺一圍，齊主從之。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler was about to return when Lady Feng the Pure Consort asked to hunt one more beat, and the Qi ruler consented.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi emperor was about to return when Lady Feng the Pure Consort asked to hunt one more beat, and he consented.

sentences.zh: 周齊王憲攻拔洪洞、永安二城，更圖進取。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Qi of Zhou captured the two cities of Hongdong and Yong'an and planned further advances.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Qi of Northern Zhou captured the two cities of Hongdong and Yong'an and planned further advances.

sentences.zh: 齊人焚橋守險，軍不得進，乃屯永安。

translations.literal: The Qi men burned the bridges and held the defiles; the army could not advance and so encamped at Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi forces burned the bridges and held the defiles; Zhou forces could not advance and encamped at Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 使永昌公椿屯雞棲原，伐柏為庵以立營。

translations.literal: He sent Duke Chun of Yongchang to encamp at Jixi Plain, felling cypresses to build shelters and establish camps.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Duke Chun of Yongchang to encamp at Jixi Plain, felling cypresses to build shelters and establish camps.

sentences.zh: 椿，廣之弟也。

translations.literal: Chun was the younger brother of Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Chun was the younger brother of Guang.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，齊主分軍萬人向千里徑，又分軍出汾水關，自帥大軍上雞棲原。

translations.literal: On guiyou, the Qi ruler divided ten thousand troops toward Qianli Pass, divided another force out through Fenshui Pass, and personally led the main army up Jixi Plain.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, the Northern Qi emperor divided ten thousand troops toward Qianli Pass, sent another force out through Fenshui Pass, and personally led the main army up Jixi Plain.

sentences.zh: 宇文盛遣人告急，齊王憲自救之。

translations.literal: Yuwen Sheng sent men to report the emergency, and Prince Xian of Qi came in person to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Sheng sent men to report the emergency, and Prince Xian of Qi came in person to rescue him.

sentences.zh: 齊師退，盛追擊，破之。

translations.literal: The Qi army withdrew. Sheng pursued and attacked, defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi army withdrew. Sheng pursued and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 俄而椿告齊師稍逼，憲復還救之。
