translations.literal: Shortly afterward Chun reported that the Qi army was pressing closer, and Xian returned again to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Chun reported that the Qi army was pressing closer, and Xian returned again to rescue him.

sentences.zh: 與齊對陳，至夜不戰。

translations.literal: They faced the Qi army in battle formation and did not fight until night.
translations.idiomatic: The two armies faced each other in battle formation and did not fight until nightfall.

sentences.zh: 會周主召憲還，憲引兵夜去。

translations.literal: Then the Zhou ruler summoned Xian back, and Xian led his troops away by night.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Zhou emperor summoned Xian back, and Xian led his troops away by night.

sentences.zh: 齊人見柏庵在，不之覺。

translations.literal: The Qi men saw the cypress shelters still standing and did not realize they had gone.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi forces saw the cypress shelters still standing and did not realize Zhou troops had gone.

sentences.zh: 明日，始知之。

translations.literal: The next day they finally learned of it.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they finally learned of it.

sentences.zh: 齊主使高阿那肱將前軍先進，仍節度諸軍。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler sent Gao Anahoug to lead the vanguard forward first and also to direct the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi emperor sent Gao Anahoug to lead the vanguard forward first and also to direct the various armies.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，周以上開府儀同大將軍安定梁士彥為晉州刺史，留精兵一萬鎮之。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Zhou appointed Liang Shiyan of Anding, Upper Palace Gate General and Pillar of State, as Governor of Jin Province and left ten thousand elite troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Northern Zhou appointed Liang Shiyan of Anding, Upper Palace Gate General and Pillar of State, as Governor of Jin Province and left ten thousand elite troops to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 十一月，己卯，齊主至平陽。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jimao, the Qi ruler arrived at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jimao, the Northern Qi emperor arrived at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 周主以齊兵新集，聲勢甚盛，且欲西還以避其鋒。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler reckoned that the Qi troops had only just assembled, their momentum was very strong, and he also wished to withdraw west to avoid their edge.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor reckoned that the Qi troops had only just assembled and their momentum was very strong, and he also wished to withdraw west to avoid their edge.

sentences.zh: 開府儀同大將軍宇文忻諫：曰「比陛下之聖武，乘敵人之荒縱，何患不克；

translations.literal: Palace Gate General and Pillar of State Yuwen Xin remonstrated: saying "Given Your Majesty's sagely martial prowess and seizing upon the enemy's wasteful indulgence, what fear is there of not conquering them;
translations.idiomatic: Palace Gate General and Pillar of State Yuwen Xin remonstrated, saying, "Given Your Majesty's sagely martial prowess and the enemy's reckless indulgence, what fear is there of not conquering them;

sentences.zh: 若使齊得令主，君臣協力，雖湯、武之勢，未易平也。

translations.literal: If Qi should obtain a worthy ruler and ruler and ministers work together, even the power of Tang and Wu would not easily subdue them.
translations.idiomatic: If Qi should obtain a worthy ruler and ruler and ministers worked together, even the power of Tang and Wu would not easily subdue them.

sentences.zh: 今主暗臣愚，士無鬥志，雖有百萬之眾，實為陛下奉耳。

translations.literal: Now the ruler is benighted and the ministers foolish; the soldiers have no will to fight. Though they number a million, they are in truth merely offerings for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Now their ruler is benighted and their ministers foolish; the soldiers have no will to fight. Though they number a million, they are in truth merely offerings for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」軍正京兆王紘曰：「齊失紀綱，於茲累世。

translations.literal: " Army Rectifier Wang Hong of Jingzhao said: "Qi has lost its discipline for generations now.
translations.idiomatic: " Army Rectifier Wang Hong of Jingzhao said, "Qi has lost its discipline for generations now.

sentences.zh: 天獎周室，一戰而扼其喉。

translations.literal: Heaven has rewarded the Zhou house—a single battle and we have their throat in our grasp.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has rewarded the Zhou house—a single battle and we have their throat in our grasp.

sentences.zh: 取亂侮亡，正在今日。

translations.literal: To seize disorder and despise a house in ruin—there is no better day than today.
translations.idiomatic: To seize disorder and despise a house in ruin—there is no better day than today.

sentences.zh: 釋之而去，臣所未諭。

translations.literal: To release them and go away—this your servant does not understand.
translations.idiomatic: To release them and withdraw—this your servant does not understand.

sentences.zh: 」周主雖善其言，竟引軍還。

translations.literal: " Though the Zhou ruler approved their words, in the end he led his army back.
translations.idiomatic: " Though the Zhou emperor approved their words, in the end he led his army back.

sentences.zh: 忻，貴之子也。

translations.literal: Xin was the son of Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was the son of Gui.

sentences.zh: 周主留齊王憲為後拒，齊師追之，憲與宇文忻各將百騎與戰，斬其驍將賀蘭豹子等，齊師乃退。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler left Prince Xian of Qi as rear guard. The Qi army pursued them. Xian and Yuwen Xin each led a hundred horsemen into battle and beheaded their fierce general Helan Baozi and others, and the Qi army then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor left Prince Xian of Qi as rear guard. The Qi army pursued them. Xian and Yuwen Xin each led a hundred horsemen into battle and beheaded their fierce general Helan Baozi and others, and the Qi army then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 憲引軍渡汾，追及周主於玉壁。

translations.literal: Xian led his army across the Fen and caught up with the Zhou ruler at Yubi.
translations.idiomatic: Xian led his army across the Fen and caught up with the Zhou emperor at Yubi.

sentences.zh: 齊師遂圍平陽，晝夜攻之。

translations.literal: The Qi army then besieged Pingyang, attacking day and night.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi army then besieged Pingyang, attacking day and night.

sentences.zh: 城中危急，樓堞皆盡，所存之城，尋仞而已。

translations.literal: Within the city the peril was extreme; the tower battlements were all gone, and what remained of the wall was only a few ren in height.
translations.idiomatic: Within the city the peril was extreme; the tower battlements were all gone, and what remained of the wall was only a few ren in height.

sentences.zh: 或短兵相接，或交馬出入。

translations.literal: At times they fought hand to hand; at times horsemen crossed in and out.
translations.idiomatic: At times they fought hand to hand; at times horsemen crossed in and out.

sentences.zh: 外援不至，眾皆震懼。

translations.literal: External relief did not arrive, and the men were all shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: External relief did not arrive, and the troops were all shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 梁士彥慷慨自若，謂將士曰：「死在今日，吾為爾先。

translations.literal: Liang Shiyan was bold and composed as ever. He told the officers and soldiers: "Today we die—I shall go before you.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shiyan was bold and composed as ever. He told the officers and soldiers, "If we die today, I shall go before you.

sentences.zh: 」於是勇烈齊奮，呼聲動地，無不一當百。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the brave and fierce rose together, their shouts shaking earth and sky, and each man fought as if a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the brave rose together, their shouts shaking earth and sky, and each man fought as if a hundred.

sentences.zh: 齊師少卻，乃令妻妾、軍民、婦女，晝夜修城，三日而就。

translations.literal: The Qi army fell back somewhat. He then ordered wives, concubines, soldiers, civilians, and women to repair the walls day and night, and in three days it was done.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi army fell back somewhat. He then ordered wives, concubines, soldiers, civilians, and women to repair the walls day and night, and in three days the work was done.

sentences.zh: 周主使齊王憲將兵六萬屯涑川，遙為平陽聲援。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler sent Prince Xian of Qi to lead sixty thousand troops to encamp at Su River, giving distant support to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor sent Prince Xian of Qi to lead sixty thousand troops to encamp at Su River, giving distant support to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 齊人作地道攻平陽，城陷十餘步，將士乘勢欲入。

translations.literal: The Qi men dug tunnels to attack Pingyang. The wall collapsed for more than ten paces, and the officers and soldiers wished to take advantage and enter.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi forces dug tunnels to attack Pingyang. The wall collapsed for more than ten paces, and the officers and soldiers wished to take advantage and enter.

sentences.zh: 齊主敕且止，召馮淑妃觀之。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler ordered them to halt for the moment and summoned Lady Feng the Pure Consort to watch.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi emperor ordered them to halt for the moment and summoned Lady Feng the Pure Consort to watch.

sentences.zh: 淑妃妝點，不時至。

translations.literal: Lady Feng was putting on her makeup and did not arrive in time.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Feng was putting on her makeup and did not arrive in time.

sentences.zh: 周人以木拒塞之，城遂不下。

translations.literal: The Zhou men blocked it with wooden barriers, and the city was not taken.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou defenders blocked the breach with wooden barriers, and the city was not taken.

sentences.zh: 舊俗相傳，晉州城西石上有聖人跡，淑妃欲往觀之。

translations.literal: By old custom it was told that on a stone west of Jin Province city were the footprints of a sage. Lady Feng wished to go and view them.
translations.idiomatic: By old custom it was said that on a stone west of Jin Province city were the footprints of a sage. Lady Feng wished to go and view them.

sentences.zh: 齊主恐弩矢及橋，乃抽攻城木造遠橋。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler feared crossbow bolts would reach the bridge, and so stripped siege timber to build a long bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi emperor feared crossbow bolts would reach the bridge, and so stripped siege timber to build a long bridge.

sentences.zh: 齊主與淑妃度橋，橋壞，至夜乃還。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler and Lady Feng crossed the bridge. The bridge broke, and they did not return until night.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi emperor and Lady Feng crossed the bridge. The bridge collapsed, and they did not return until night.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，周主還長安。

translations.literal: On guisi, the Zhou ruler returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, the Zhou emperor returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 甲午，復下詔，以齊人圍晉州，更帥諸軍擊之。

translations.literal: On jiawu, he again issued an edict that, because the Qi men were besieging Jin Province, he would again lead the various armies to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, he again issued an edict that, because the Qi forces were besieging Jin Province, he would again lead the various armies to strike them.

sentences.zh: 丙申，縱齊降人使還。

translations.literal: On bingshen, he released Qi prisoners to let them return.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, he released Qi prisoners to let them return.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，周主發長安；

translations.literal: On dingyou, the Zhou ruler departed from Chang'an;
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, the Zhou emperor departed from Chang'an;

sentences.zh: 壬寅，濟河，與諸軍合。

translations.literal: on renyin he crossed the river and joined with the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: on renyin he crossed the river and joined with the various armies.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丁未，周主至高顯，遣齊王憲帥所部先向平陽。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on dingwei, the Zhou ruler reached Gaoxian and sent Prince Xian of Qi to lead his division first toward Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on dingwei, the Zhou emperor reached Gaoxian and sent Prince Xian of Qi to lead his division first toward Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 戊申，周主至平陽，庚戌，諸軍總集，凡八萬人，稍進，逼城置陳，東西二十餘里。

translations.literal: On wushen the Zhou ruler reached Pingyang. On gengxu the various armies assembled in all—eighty thousand men. They advanced gradually, pressed close to the city, and set battle lines extending east and west for more than twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen the Zhou emperor reached Pingyang. On gengxu the various armies assembled in all—eighty thousand men. They advanced gradually, pressed close to the city, and set battle lines extending east and west for more than twenty li.

sentences.zh: 先是齊人恐周師猝至，於城南穿塹，自喬山屬於汾水；

translations.literal: Previously, fearing that Zhou troops might arrive suddenly, the Qi men dug a ditch south of the city, running from Qiaoshan to the Fen River;
translations.idiomatic: Previously, fearing that Zhou troops might arrive suddenly, the Qi forces dug a ditch south of the city, running from Qiaoshan to the Fen River;

sentences.zh: 齊主大出兵，陳於塹北，周主命齊王憲馳往觀之。

translations.literal: the Qi ruler massed a great army and arrayed it north of the ditch. The Zhou ruler ordered Prince Xian of Qi to ride quickly to observe it.
translations.idiomatic: the Northern Qi emperor massed a great army and arrayed it north of the ditch. The Zhou emperor ordered Prince Xian of Qi to ride quickly to observe it.

sentences.zh: 憲覆命曰：「易與耳，請破之而後食。

translations.literal: Xian reported back: "They are easy to deal with. Allow us to defeat them before we eat.
translations.idiomatic: Xian reported back, "They are easy to deal with. Allow us to defeat them before we eat.

sentences.zh: 」周主悅，曰：「如汝言，吾無憂矣！

translations.literal: " The Zhou ruler was pleased and said: "As you say, I have no worries!
translations.idiomatic: " The Zhou emperor was pleased and said, "As you say, I have no worries!

sentences.zh: 」周主乘常御馬，從數人巡陳，所至輒呼主帥姓名慰勉之。

translations.literal: " The Zhou ruler rode his usual mount with only a few attendants and inspected the battle lines. Wherever he went he called out commanders by name and encouraged them.
translations.idiomatic: " The Zhou emperor rode his usual mount with only a few attendants and inspected the battle lines. Wherever he went he called out commanders by name and encouraged them.

sentences.zh: 將士喜於見知，鹹思自奮。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers were pleased to be recognized and all wished to exert themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The officers and soldiers were pleased to be recognized and all wished to exert themselves.

sentences.zh: 將戰，有司請換馬。

translations.literal: Just before battle, the officials requested that he change horses.
translations.idiomatic: Just before battle, the officials requested that he change horses.

sentences.zh: 周主曰：「朕獨乘良馬，欲何之！

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler said: "If I alone ride a fine horse, where would I go!
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor said, "If I alone ride a fine horse, where would I go!

sentences.zh: 」周主欲薄齊師，礙塹而止。

translations.literal: " The Zhou ruler wished to press close to the Qi army but was blocked by the ditch and halted.
translations.idiomatic: " The Zhou emperor wished to press close to the Qi army but was blocked by the ditch and halted.

sentences.zh: 自旦至申，相持不決。

translations.literal: From dawn until shen hour they faced each other without resolution.
translations.idiomatic: From dawn until shen hour they faced each other without resolution.

sentences.zh: 齊主謂高阿那肱曰：「戰是邪？

translations.literal: The Qi ruler said to Gao Anahoug: "Shall we fight?
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi emperor said to Gao Anahoug, "Shall we fight?

sentences.zh: 不戰是邪？

translations.literal: Shall we not fight?
translations.idiomatic: Shall we not fight?

sentences.zh: 」阿那肱曰：「吾兵雖多，堪戰者不過十萬，病傷及繞城樵爨者復三分居一。

translations.literal: " Anahoug said: "Though our troops are many, those fit to fight are no more than one hundred thousand. The sick, wounded, and those gathering firewood and cooking around the city walls account for another third.
translations.idiomatic: " Anahoug said, "Though our troops are many, those fit to fight are no more than one hundred thousand. The sick, wounded, and those gathering firewood and cooking around the city walls account for another third.

sentences.zh: 昔攻玉壁，援軍來即退。

translations.literal: In the past when we attacked Yubi, we withdrew as soon as relief arrived.
translations.idiomatic: In the past when we attacked Yubi, we withdrew as soon as relief arrived.

sentences.zh: 今日將士，豈勝神武時邪！

translations.literal: How can today's officers and soldiers compare with those in the time of the Divine Martial Emperor!
translations.idiomatic: How can today's officers and soldiers compare with those in the time of the Divine Martial Emperor!

sentences.zh: 不如勿戰，卻守高梁橋。

translations.literal: Better not to fight and instead withdraw to hold Gaoliang Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Better not to fight and instead withdraw to hold Gaoliang Bridge.

sentences.zh: 」安吐根曰：「一撮許賊，馬上刺取，擲著汾水中耳！

translations.literal: " An Tugen said: "That handful of bandits—spear them from horseback and toss them into the Fen River!
translations.idiomatic: " An Tugen said, "That handful of bandits—spear them from horseback and toss them into the Fen River!

sentences.zh: 」齊主意未決。

translations.literal: " The Qi ruler's mind was not yet decided.
translations.idiomatic: " The Northern Qi emperor's mind was not yet decided.

sentences.zh: 諸內參曰：「彼亦天子，我亦天子。

translations.literal: The various inner attendants said: "He too is Son of Heaven, and we too are Sons of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The various inner attendants said, "He too is Son of Heaven, and we too are Sons of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 彼尚能遠來，我何為守塹示弱！

translations.literal: He can come from far away—why should we hold a ditch and show weakness!
translations.idiomatic: He has come from far away—why should we hold a ditch and show weakness!

sentences.zh: 」齊主曰：「此言是也。

translations.literal: " The Qi ruler said: "These words are correct.
translations.idiomatic: " The Northern Qi emperor said, "These words are correct.

sentences.zh: 」於是填塹南引。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they filled the ditch and advanced south.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon they filled the ditch and advanced south.

sentences.zh: 周主大喜，勒諸軍擊之。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler was greatly pleased and urged the various armies to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor was greatly pleased and urged the various armies to attack them.

sentences.zh: 兵才合，齊主與馮淑妃並騎觀戰。

translations.literal: The armies had only just joined battle when the Qi ruler and Lady Feng the Pure Consort rode side by side to watch the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: The armies had only just joined battle when the Northern Qi emperor and Lady Feng the Pure Consort rode side by side to watch the fighting.

sentences.zh: 東偏小卻，淑妃怖曰：「軍敗矣！

translations.literal: The eastern wing fell back slightly. Lady Feng said in fear: "The army is defeated!
translations.idiomatic: The eastern wing fell back slightly. Lady Feng said in fear, "The army is defeated!

sentences.zh: 」錄尚書事城陽王穆提婆曰：「大家去！

translations.literal: " Chief Secretary of State Affairs Mutipo, Prince of Chengyang, said: "Your Majesty, go!
translations.idiomatic: " Chief Secretary of State Affairs Mutipo, Prince of Chengyang, said, "Your Majesty, go!

sentences.zh: 大家去！

translations.literal: Your Majesty, go!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, go!

sentences.zh: 」齊主即以淑妃奔高梁橋。

translations.literal: " The Qi ruler thereupon fled with Lady Feng to Gaoliang Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: " The Northern Qi emperor thereupon fled with Lady Feng to Gaoliang Bridge.

sentences.zh: 開府儀同三司奚長諫曰：「半進半退，戰之常體。

translations.literal: Palace Gate General of the Third Rank Xi Chang remonstrated: "Advancing half and retreating half is the normal pattern of battle.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Gate General of the Third Rank Xi Chang remonstrated, "Advancing half and retreating half is the normal pattern of battle.

sentences.zh: 今兵眾全整，未有虧傷，陛下捨此安之！

translations.literal: Now the troops are wholly intact and have suffered no losses. Where will Your Majesty go if you abandon this place!
translations.idiomatic: Now the troops are wholly intact and have suffered no losses. Where will Your Majesty go if you abandon this place!

sentences.zh: 馬足一動，人情駭亂，不可復振。

translations.literal: Once the horses' hooves move, men's hearts will be thrown into panic and cannot be rallied again.
translations.idiomatic: Once the horses' hooves move, men's hearts will be thrown into panic and cannot be rallied again.

sentences.zh: 願速還安慰之！

translations.literal: I beg you to return quickly and reassure them!
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to return quickly and reassure them!

sentences.zh: 」武衛張常山自後至，亦曰：「軍尋收訖，甚完整。

translations.literal: " Guard Commander Zhang Changshan arrived from the rear and also said: "The army is about to regroup and is still very intact.
translations.idiomatic: " Guard Commander Zhang Changshan arrived from the rear and also said, "The army is about to regroup and is still very intact.

sentences.zh: 圍城兵亦不動。

translations.literal: The troops besieging the city have not moved either.
translations.idiomatic: The troops besieging the city have not moved either.

sentences.zh: 至尊宜回。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should return.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should return.

sentences.zh: 不信臣言，乞將內參往視。

translations.literal: If you do not believe my words, I beg to take the inner attendants to go and see.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not believe my words, I beg to take the inner attendants to go and see for themselves.

sentences.zh: 」齊主將從之。

translations.literal: " The Qi ruler was about to follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: " The Northern Qi emperor was about to follow this advice.

sentences.zh: 穆提婆引齊主肘曰：「此言難信。

translations.literal: Mutipo pulled the Qi ruler by the elbow and said: "These words are hard to believe.
translations.idiomatic: Mutipo pulled the Northern Qi emperor by the elbow and said, "These words are hard to believe.

sentences.zh: 」齊主遂以淑妃北走。

translations.literal: " The Qi ruler thereupon fled north with Lady Feng.
translations.idiomatic: " The Northern Qi emperor thereupon fled north with Lady Feng.

sentences.zh: 齊師大潰，死者萬餘人，軍資器械，數百里間，委棄山積。

translations.literal: The Qi army broke in great rout. More than ten thousand men died, and military supplies and equipment were abandoned in heaps for hundreds of li.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi army broke in great rout. More than ten thousand men died, and military supplies and equipment were abandoned in heaps for hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 安德王延宗獨全軍而還。

translations.literal: Prince Yan Zong of Ande alone brought his whole army back intact.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yan Zong of Ande alone brought his whole army back intact.

sentences.zh: 齊主至洪洞，淑妃方以粉鏡自玩，後聲亂，唱賊至，於是復走。

translations.literal: When the Qi ruler reached Hongdong, Lady Feng was just amusing herself with a powder mirror. Then shouts rose from behind crying that bandits had arrived, and so he fled again.
translations.idiomatic: When the Northern Qi emperor reached Hongdong, Lady Feng was just amusing herself with a powder mirror. Then shouts rose from behind crying that bandits had arrived, and so he fled again.

sentences.zh: 先是齊主以淑妃為有功勳，將立為左皇后，遣內參詣晉陽取皇后服御禕翟等。

translations.literal: Previously the Qi ruler, because Lady Feng had rendered meritorious service, was about to establish her as Left Empress and had sent inner attendants to Jinyang to fetch empress robes, ceremonial regalia, and feathered banners.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the Northern Qi emperor, because Lady Feng had rendered meritorious service, was about to establish her as Left Empress and had sent inner attendants to Jinyang to fetch empress robes, ceremonial regalia, and feathered banners.

sentences.zh: 至是，遇於中塗，齊主為按轡，命淑妃著之，然後去。

translations.literal: At this time they met them on the road. The Qi ruler reined in his horse, ordered Lady Feng to put them on, and only then went on.
translations.idiomatic: At this time they met them on the road. The Northern Qi emperor reined in his horse, ordered Lady Feng to put them on, and only then went on.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，周主入平陽。

translations.literal: On xinhai, the Zhou ruler entered Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, the Zhou emperor entered Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 梁士彥見周主，持周主須而泣曰：「臣幾不見陛下！

translations.literal: Liang Shiyan saw the Zhou ruler, took hold of his beard and wept, saying: "Your servant nearly did not see Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shiyan saw the Zhou emperor, took hold of his beard and wept, saying, "Your servant nearly did not see Your Majesty!

sentences.zh: 」周主亦為之流涕。

translations.literal: " The Zhou ruler also wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: " The Zhou emperor also wept for him.

sentences.zh: 周主以將士疲倦，欲引還。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler, because the officers and soldiers were weary, wished to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor, because the officers and soldiers were weary, wished to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 士彥叩馬諫曰：「今齊師遁散，眾心皆動。

translations.literal: Shiyan knocked on the horse and remonstrated: "Now the Qi army has scattered in flight and every heart is shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan knocked on the horse and remonstrated, "Now the Qi army has scattered in flight and every heart is shaken.

sentences.zh: 因其懼而攻之，其勢必舉。

translations.literal: If we attack them while they are afraid, the enterprise is sure to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: If we attack them while they are afraid, the enterprise is sure to succeed.

sentences.zh: 」周主從之，執其手曰：「余得晉州，為平齊之基，若不固守，則大事不成。

translations.literal: " The Zhou ruler followed his advice and took his hand, saying: "I gained Jin Province as the foundation for pacifying Qi. If it is not firmly held, the great enterprise will not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: " The Zhou emperor followed his advice and took his hand, saying, "I gained Jin Province as the foundation for pacifying Qi. If it is not firmly held, the great enterprise will not succeed.

sentences.zh: 朕無前憂，唯慮後變，汝善為我守之！

translations.literal: I have no worry about what lies before, only fear of changes afterward. You must hold it well for me!
translations.idiomatic: I have no worry about what lies before, only fear of changes afterward. You must hold it well for me!

sentences.zh: 」遂帥諸將追齊師。

translations.literal: " He thereupon led the various generals in pursuit of the Qi army.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon led the various generals in pursuit of the Qi army.

sentences.zh: 諸將固請西還，周主曰：「縱敵患生。

translations.literal: The generals firmly requested to return west. The Zhou ruler said: "To let the enemy go breeds future trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The generals firmly requested to return west. The Zhou emperor said, "To let the enemy go breeds future trouble.

sentences.zh: 卿等若疑，朕將獨往。

translations.literal: If you are doubtful, I shall go alone.
translations.idiomatic: If you are doubtful, I shall go alone.

sentences.zh: 」諸將乃不敢言。

translations.literal: " The generals then did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: " The generals then did not dare speak.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，至汾水關。

translations.literal: On guichou, they reached Fenshui Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, they reached Fenshui Pass.

sentences.zh: 齊主入晉陽，憂懼不知所之。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler entered Jinyang, anxious and fearful, not knowing where to go.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi emperor entered Jinyang, anxious and fearful, not knowing where to go.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，齊大赦。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Qi proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Northern Qi proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 齊主問計於朝臣，皆曰：「宜省賦息役，以慰民心；

translations.literal: The Qi ruler asked the court ministers for plans. All said: "Taxes and corvée labor should be reduced to comfort the people's hearts;
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi emperor asked the court ministers for plans. All said, "Taxes and corvée labor should be reduced to comfort the people's hearts;

sentences.zh: 收遺兵，背城死戰，以安社稷。

translations.literal: gather the scattered troops, fight to the death with the city at your back, and thereby secure the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: gather the scattered troops, fight to the death with the city at your back, and thereby secure the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 」齊主欲留安德王延宗、廣寧王孝珩守晉陽，自向北朔州。

translations.literal: " The Qi ruler wished to leave Prince Yan Zong of Ande and Prince Xiaoheng of Guangning to hold Jinyang while he himself went north to Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: " The Northern Qi emperor wished to leave Prince Yan Zong of Ande and Prince Xiaoheng of Guangning to hold Jinyang while he himself went north to Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 若晉陽不守，則奔突厥，群臣皆以為不可，帝不從。

translations.literal: If Jinyang could not be held, he would flee to the Turks. The ministers all considered this impossible, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: If Jinyang could not be held, he would flee to the Turks. The ministers all considered this impossible, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 開府儀同三司賀拔伏恩等宿衛近臣三十餘人西奔周軍，周主封賞各有差。

translations.literal: More than thirty close attendants on palace guard duty, including Palace Gate General of the Third Rank Heba Fu'en, fled west to the Zhou army. The Zhou ruler enfeoffed and rewarded each according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: More than thirty close attendants on palace guard duty, including Palace Gate General of the Third Rank Heba Fu'en, fled west to the Zhou army. The Zhou emperor enfeoffed and rewarded each according to merit.

sentences.zh: 高阿那肱所部兵尚一萬，守高壁，餘眾保洛女砦。

translations.literal: The troops under Gao Anahoug still numbered ten thousand. He held Gaobi, while the rest of the men defended Luonü Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: The troops under Gao Anahoug still numbered ten thousand. He held Gaobi, while the rest of the men defended Luonü Stockade.

sentences.zh: 周主引軍向高壁，阿那肱望風退走。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler led his army toward Gaobi. Anahoug fled at the sight of them.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor led his army toward Gaobi. Anahoug fled at the sight of them.

sentences.zh: 齊王憲攻洛女砦，拔之。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Qi attacked Luonü Stockade and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Qi attacked Luonü Stockade and captured it.

sentences.zh: 有軍士告稱阿那肱遣臣招引西軍，齊主令侍中斛律孝卿檢校，孝卿以為妄。

translations.literal: A soldier reported that Anahoug had sent him to lure the western army. The Qi ruler ordered Palace Attendant Hulu Xiaqing to investigate. Xiaqing considered it false.
translations.idiomatic: A soldier reported that Anahoug had sent him to lure the western army. The Northern Qi emperor ordered Palace Attendant Hulu Xiaqing to investigate. Xiaqing considered it false.

sentences.zh: 還，至晉陽，阿那肱腹心復告阿那肱謀反，又以為妄，斬之。

translations.literal: On returning to Jinyang, Anahoug's confidants again reported that Anahoug was plotting rebellion. Again it was considered false, and they were executed.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to Jinyang, Anahoug's confidants again reported that Anahoug was plotting rebellion. Again it was considered false, and they were executed.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，齊主詔安德王延宗、廣寧王孝珩募兵。

translations.literal: On yimao, the Qi ruler ordered Prince Yan Zong of Ande and Prince Xiaoheng of Guangning to recruit troops.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, the Northern Qi emperor ordered Prince Yan Zong of Ande and Prince Xiaoheng of Guangning to recruit troops.

sentences.zh: 延宗入見，齊主告以欲向北朔州，延宗泣諫，不從，密遣左右先送皇太后、太子於北朔州。

translations.literal: Yan Zong came in to see him. The Qi ruler told him of his wish to go north to Shuozhou. Yan Zong remonstrated with tears but was not heeded. Secretly he sent attendants ahead to escort the Empress Dowager and Crown Prince to northern Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zong came in to see him. The Northern Qi emperor told him of his wish to go north to Shuozhou. Yan Zong remonstrated with tears but was not heeded. Secretly he sent attendants ahead to escort the Empress Dowager and Crown Prince to northern Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，周主與齊王憲會於介休。

translations.literal: On bingchen, the Zhou ruler joined Prince Xian of Qi at Jiexiu.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, the Zhou emperor joined Prince Xian of Qi at Jiexiu.

sentences.zh: 齊開府儀同三司韓建業舉城降，以為上柱國，封郇公。

translations.literal: Han Jianye, Palace Gate General of the Third Rank of Qi, surrendered the whole city. He was made Upper Pillar of State and enfeoffed as Duke of Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jianye, Palace Gate General of the Third Rank of Qi, surrendered the whole city. He was made Upper Pillar of State and enfeoffed as Duke of Xun.

sentences.zh: 是夜，齊主欲遁去，諸將不從。

translations.literal: That night the Qi ruler wished to slip away, but the generals would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: That night the Northern Qi emperor wished to slip away, but the generals would not follow.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，周師至晉陽。

translations.literal: On dingsi, the Zhou army reached Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, the Zhou army reached Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 齊主復大赦，改元隆化。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler again proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Longhua.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi emperor again proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Longhua.

sentences.zh: 以安德王延宗為相國、并州刺史，總山西兵，謂曰：「并州兄自取之，兒今去矣！

translations.literal: He appointed Prince Yan Zong of Ande as Chancellor and Governor of Bing Province to command the troops of the western mountains, saying to him: "Bing Province, elder brother, take for yourself—I, your son, am leaving now!
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Prince Yan Zong of Ande as Chancellor and Governor of Bing Province to command the troops of the western mountains, saying to him, "Bing Province, elder brother, take for yourself—I am leaving now!

sentences.zh: 」延宗曰：「陛下為社稷勿動。

translations.literal: " Yan Zong said: "Your Majesty, for the sake of the altars of state, do not move.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan Zong said, "Your Majesty, for the sake of the altars of state, do not move.

sentences.zh: 臣為陛下出死力戰，必能破之。

translations.literal: Your servant will exert himself unto death for Your Majesty and is sure to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant will exert himself unto death for Your Majesty and is sure to defeat them.

sentences.zh: 」穆提婆曰：「至尊計已成，王不得輒沮！

translations.literal: " Mutipo said: "His Majesty's plan is already settled. Your Highness must not rashly discourage it!
translations.idiomatic: " Mutipo said, "His Majesty's plan is already settled. Your Highness must not rashly discourage it!

sentences.zh: 」齊主乃夜斬五龍門而出，欲奔突厥，從官多散。

translations.literal: " That night the Qi ruler cut through Wulong Gate and went out, intending to flee to the Turks. Most of his attendants scattered.
translations.idiomatic: " That night the Northern Qi emperor cut through Wulong Gate and went out, intending to flee to the Turks. Most of his attendants scattered.

sentences.zh: 領軍梅勝郎叩馬諫，乃回向鄴。

translations.literal: Army Director Mei Sheng remonstrated by knocking on the horse, and he thereupon turned back toward Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Army Director Mei Sheng remonstrated by knocking on the horse, and he thereupon turned back toward Ye.

sentences.zh: 時唯高阿那肱等十餘騎從，廣寧王孝珩、襄城王彥道繼至，得數十人與俱。

translations.literal: At the time only a dozen or so horsemen including Gao Anahoug followed him. Prince Xiaoheng of Guangning and Prince Yandao of Xiangcheng arrived afterward, and he had several dozen men with him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time only a dozen or so horsemen including Gao Anahoug followed him. Prince Xiaoheng of Guangning and Prince Yandao of Xiangcheng arrived afterward, and he had several dozen men with him.

sentences.zh: 穆提婆西奔周軍，陸令萱自殺，家屬皆誅沒。

translations.literal: Mutipo fled west to the Zhou army. Lu Lingxuan killed herself, and her family members were all executed and their property confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Mutipo fled west to the Zhou army. Lu Lingxuan killed herself, and her family members were all executed and their property confiscated.

sentences.zh: 周主以提婆為柱國、宜州刺史。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler appointed Tipo as Pillar of State and Governor of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor appointed Tipo as Pillar of State and Governor of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 下詔諭齊群臣曰：「若妙盡人謀，深達天命，官榮爵賞，各有加隆。

translations.literal: An edict was issued to instruct the Qi ministers: "If you fully employ human counsel and deeply comprehend Heaven's mandate, official honors and noble rewards will each be increased.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued to instruct the Qi ministers, "If you fully employ human counsel and deeply comprehend Heaven's mandate, official honors and noble rewards will each be increased.

sentences.zh: 或我之將卒，逃逸彼朝，無問貴賤，皆從蕩滌。

translations.literal: If any of our officers and soldiers have fled to that court, regardless of rank, they will all be swept away.
translations.idiomatic: If any of our officers and soldiers have fled to that court, regardless of rank, they will all be swept away.

sentences.zh: 」自是齊臣降者相繼。

translations.literal: " From this time Qi ministers surrendered one after another.
translations.idiomatic: " From this time Qi ministers surrendered one after another.

sentences.zh: 初，齊高祖為魏丞相，以唐邕典外兵曹，太原白建典騎兵曹，皆以善書計、工簿帳受委任。

translations.literal: Initially, when the Qi Founding Emperor was Chancellor of Wei, he put Tang Yong in charge of the Outer Military Office and Bai Jian of Taiyuan in charge of the Cavalry Office. Both were entrusted because they were skilled at writing accounts and adept at ledgers.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, when the Qi Founding Emperor was Chancellor of Wei, he put Tang Yong in charge of the Outer Military Office and Bai Jian of Taiyuan in charge of the Cavalry Office. Both were entrusted because they were skilled at writing accounts and adept at ledgers.

sentences.zh: 及齊受禪，諸司鹹歸尚書；

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, the various offices all came under the Ministry of State Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, the various offices all came under the Ministry of State Affairs;

sentences.zh: 唯二曹不廢，更名二省。

translations.literal: only these two offices were not abolished and were renamed the Two Departments.
translations.idiomatic: only these two offices were not abolished and were renamed the Two Departments.

sentences.zh: 邕官至錄尚書事，建官至中書令，常典二省，世稱「唐、白」。

translations.literal: Yong rose to Chief Secretary of State Affairs and Jian to Director of the Palace Secretariat. They regularly managed the Two Departments and were known in their age as "Tang and Bai."
translations.idiomatic: Yong rose to Chief Secretary of State Affairs and Jian to Director of the Palace Secretariat. They regularly managed the Two Departments and were known in their age as "Tang and Bai."

sentences.zh: 邕兼領度支，與高阿那肱有隙，阿那肱譖之，齊主敕侍中斛律孝卿總知騎兵、度支。

translations.literal: Yong also concurrently headed the Revenue Office. He had a rift with Gao Anahoug, who slandered him. The Qi ruler ordered Palace Attendant Hulu Xiaqing to take overall charge of cavalry and revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Yong also concurrently headed the Revenue Office. He had a rift with Gao Anahoug, who slandered him. The Northern Qi emperor ordered Palace Attendant Hulu Xiaqing to take overall charge of cavalry and revenue.

sentences.zh: 孝卿事多專決，不復詢稟。

translations.literal: Xiaqing decided many matters on his own and no longer sought instructions.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaqing decided many matters on his own and no longer sought instructions.

sentences.zh: 邕自以宿舊習事，為孝卿所輕，意甚鬱鬱。

translations.literal: Yong, considering himself an old hand versed in affairs, felt slighted by Xiaqing and was deeply depressed.
translations.idiomatic: Yong, considering himself an old hand versed in affairs, felt slighted by Xiaqing and was deeply depressed.

sentences.zh: 及齊主還鄴，邕遂留晉陽。

translations.literal: When the Qi ruler returned to Ye, Yong remained at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Northern Qi emperor returned to Ye, Yong remained at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 并州將帥請於安德王延宗曰：「王不為天子，諸人實不能為王出死力。

translations.literal: The generals of Bing Province petitioned Prince Yan Zong of Ande: "If Your Highness is not Son of Heaven, these men truly cannot exert themselves unto death for you.
translations.idiomatic: The generals of Bing Province petitioned Prince Yan Zong of Ande, "If Your Highness is not Son of Heaven, these men truly cannot exert themselves unto death for you.

sentences.zh: 」延宗不得已，戊午，即皇帝位。

translations.literal: " Yan Zong had no choice. On wuwu he ascended the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan Zong had no choice. On wuwu he ascended the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 下詔曰：「武平孱弱，政由宦豎，斬關夜遁，莫知所之。

translations.literal: An edict was issued: "The Wuping reign was feeble; government was controlled by eunuchs. He cut through the gate and fled by night—no one knows where he went.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued, "The Wuping reign was feeble; government was controlled by eunuchs. He cut through the gate and fled by night—no one knows where he went.

sentences.zh: 王公卿士，猥見推逼，今祗承寶位。

translations.literal: Princes, dukes, and ministers have unworthily pressed me, and I now reverently accept the precious throne.
translations.idiomatic: Princes, dukes, and ministers have unworthily pressed me, and I now reverently accept the throne.

sentences.zh: 」大赦，改元德昌。

translations.literal: " A general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name changed to Dechang.
translations.idiomatic: " A general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name changed to Dechang.

sentences.zh: 以晉昌王唐邕為宰相，齊昌王莫多婁敬顯、沭陽王和阿干子、右衛大將軍段暢、開府儀同三司韓骨胡等為將帥。

translations.literal: Prince Tang Yong of Jinchang was made Chancellor; Prince Modou Jingxian of Qichang, Prince A Ganzi of Shuyang, Right Guard General Duan Chang, Palace Gate General of the Third Rank Han Guhu, and others were made generals.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tang Yong of Jinchang was made Chancellor; Prince Modou Jingxian of Qichang, Prince A Ganzi of Shuyang, Right Guard General Duan Chang, Palace Gate General of the Third Rank Han Guhu, and others were made generals.

sentences.zh: 敬顯，貸文之子也。

translations.literal: Jingxian was the son of Daiwen.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian was the son of Daiwen.

sentences.zh: 眾聞之，不召而至者，前後相屬。

translations.literal: When the masses heard of it, those who came without being summoned followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: When the masses heard of it, those who came without being summoned followed one after another.

sentences.zh: 延宗發府藏及後宮美女以賜將士，籍沒內參十餘家。

translations.literal: Yan Zong opened the treasury stores and the palace beauties to reward the officers and soldiers, and confiscated the property of more than ten inner-attendant families.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zong opened the treasury stores and distributed palace beauties to reward the officers and soldiers, and confiscated the property of more than ten inner-attendant families.

sentences.zh: 齊主聞之，謂近臣曰：「我寧使周得并州，不欲安德得之。

translations.literal: When the Qi ruler heard of it, he told his close attendants: "I would rather let Zhou take Bing Province than let Ande have it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Northern Qi emperor heard of it, he told his close attendants, "I would rather let Zhou take Bing Province than let Ande have it.

sentences.zh: 」左右曰：「理然。

translations.literal: " His attendants said: "That is reasonable.
translations.idiomatic: " His attendants said, "That is reasonable.

sentences.zh: 」延宗見士卒，皆親執手稱名，流涕嗚咽，眾爭為死；

translations.literal: " When Yan Zong saw the soldiers, he personally took each by the hand and called him by name, weeping and sobbing. The men vied to die for him;
translations.idiomatic: " When Yan Zong saw the soldiers, he personally took each by the hand and called him by name, weeping and sobbing. The men vied to die for him;

sentences.zh: 童兒女子，亦乘屋攘袂，投磚石以禦敵。

translations.literal: boys and girls too climbed onto roofs, rolled up their sleeves, and threw bricks and stones to repel the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: boys and girls too climbed onto roofs, rolled up their sleeves, and threw bricks and stones to repel the enemy.

sentences.zh: 己未，周主至晉陽。

translations.literal: On jiwei, the Zhou ruler reached Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, the Zhou emperor reached Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 庚申，齊主入鄴。

translations.literal: On gengshen, the Qi ruler entered Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, the Northern Qi emperor entered Ye.

sentences.zh: 周軍圍晉陽，四合如黑雲。

translations.literal: The Zhou army besieged Jinyang, closing in on all four sides like a black cloud.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou army besieged Jinyang, closing in on all four sides like a black cloud.

sentences.zh: 安德王延宗命莫多婁敬顯、韓骨胡拒城南，和阿干子、段暢拒城東，自帥眾拒齊王憲於城北。

translations.literal: Prince Yan Zong of Ande ordered Modou Jingxian and Han Guhu to hold the south of the city; A Ganzi and Duan Chang to hold the east; and he personally led troops to hold Prince Xian of Qi at the north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yan Zong of Ande ordered Modou Jingxian and Han Guhu to hold the south of the city; A Ganzi and Duan Chang to hold the east; and he personally led troops to hold Prince Xian of Qi at the north of the city.

sentences.zh: 延宗素肥，前如偃，後如伏，人常笑之。

translations.literal: Yan Zong had always been fat—his front like a reclining figure, his back like one lying prone—and people often laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zong had always been fat—his front like a reclining figure, his back like one lying prone—and people often laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 至是，奮大槊往來督戰，勁捷若飛，所向無前。

translations.literal: At this time he wielded a great spear back and forth to direct the fighting, swift and agile as if flying, unstoppable wherever he went.
translations.idiomatic: At this time he wielded a great spear back and forth to direct the fighting, swift and agile as if flying, unstoppable wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 和阿干子、段暢以千騎奔周軍。

translations.literal: A Ganzi and Duan Chang fled with a thousand horsemen to the Zhou army.
translations.idiomatic: A Ganzi and Duan Chang fled with a thousand horsemen to the Zhou army.

sentences.zh: 周主攻東門，際昏，遂入之，進焚佛寺。

translations.literal: The Zhou army attacked the east gate. At dusk they entered it and advanced to burn the Buddhist temple.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou army attacked the east gate. At dusk they entered it and advanced to burn the Buddhist temple.

sentences.zh: 延宗、敬顯自門入，夾擊之。

translations.literal: Yan Zong and Jingxian entered through the gate and attacked them from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zong and Jingxian entered through the gate and attacked them from both sides.

sentences.zh: 周師大亂，爭門，相填壓，塞路不得進。

translations.literal: The Zhou army fell into great disorder, struggling for the gate, trampling one another, blocking the road so they could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou army fell into great disorder, struggling for the gate, trampling one another, blocking the road so they could not advance.

sentences.zh: 齊人從後斫刺，死者二千餘人。

translations.literal: The Qi men hacked and stabbed from behind, and more than two thousand men died.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi forces hacked and stabbed from behind, and more than two thousand men died.

sentences.zh: 周主左右略盡，自拔無路。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler's attendants were nearly all gone, and he could find no way to extricate himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor's attendants were nearly all gone, and he could find no way to extricate himself.

sentences.zh: 承御上士張壽牽馬首，賀拔伏恩以鞭拂其後，崎嶇得出。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Senior Gentleman Zhang Shou seized the horse's head, and Heba Fu'en whipped its hindquarters. Over rough ground they finally got out.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Senior Gentleman Zhang Shou seized the horse's head, and Heba Fu'en whipped its hindquarters. Over rough ground they finally got out.

sentences.zh: 齊人奮擊，幾中之。

translations.literal: The Qi men struck fiercely and nearly hit him.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi forces struck fiercely and nearly hit him.

sentences.zh: 城東道□厄曲，伏恩及降者皮子信導之，僅得免，時已四更。

translations.literal: The road east of the city was narrow, perilous and winding. Fu'en and the defector Pizi Xin guided him, and he barely escaped. It was already the fourth watch.
translations.idiomatic: The road east of the city was narrow, perilous and winding. Fu'en and the defector Pizi Xin guided him, and he barely escaped. It was already the fourth watch.

sentences.zh: 延宗謂周主為亂兵所殺，使於積屍中求長鬣者，不得。

translations.literal: Yan Zong thought the Zhou ruler had been killed by the disorderly troops and had men search among the heaped corpses for one with long whiskers, but they did not find him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zong thought the Zhou emperor had been killed by the disorderly troops and had men search among the heaped corpses for one with long whiskers, but they did not find him.

sentences.zh: 時齊人既捷。

translations.literal: By then the Qi men had already won.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Qi forces had already won.

sentences.zh: 入坊飲酒，盡醉臥，延宗不復能整。

translations.literal: They entered the wards to drink, all drunk and lying down, and Yan Zong could no longer restore order.
translations.idiomatic: They entered the wards to drink, all drunk and lying down, and Yan Zong could no longer restore order.

sentences.zh: 周主出城，饑甚，欲遁去，諸將亦多勸之還。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler left the city, was very hungry, and wished to slip away. Many of the generals also urged him to return.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor left the city, was very hungry, and wished to slip away. Many of the generals also urged him to return.

sentences.zh: 宇文忻勃然進曰：「陛下自克晉州，乘勝至此。

translations.literal: Yuwen Xin stepped forward angrily and said: "Your Majesty, since capturing Jin Province, has ridden victory to this point.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Xin stepped forward angrily and said, "Your Majesty, since capturing Jin Province, has ridden victory to this point.

sentences.zh: 今偽主奔波，關東響震，自古行兵，未有若斯之盛。

translations.literal: Now the false ruler is in flight, and the lands east of the pass tremble at the news. Since ancient times in campaigning, there has never been such grandeur.
translations.idiomatic: Now the false ruler is in flight, and the lands east of the pass tremble at the news. Since ancient times in campaigning, there has never been such grandeur.

sentences.zh: 昨日破城，將士輕敵，微有不利，何足為懷！

translations.literal: Yesterday we broke the city; the officers and soldiers grew contemptuous of the enemy and suffered a slight setback—what is there to brood over!
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday we broke the city; the officers and soldiers grew contemptuous of the enemy and suffered a slight setback—what is there to brood over!

sentences.zh: 丈夫當死中求生，敗中取勝。

translations.literal: A man should seek life amid death and seize victory from defeat.
translations.idiomatic: A man should seek life amid death and seize victory from defeat.

sentences.zh: 今破竹之勢已成，奈何棄之而去！

translations.literal: Now the momentum of splitting bamboo is already formed—how can we abandon it and go away!
translations.idiomatic: Now the momentum of splitting bamboo is already formed—how can we abandon it and withdraw!

sentences.zh: 」齊王憲、柱國王誼亦以為去必不免，段暢等又盛言城內空虛。

translations.literal: " Prince Xian of Qi and Pillar of State Wang Yi also thought that to leave would surely mean no escape. Duan Chang and others further declared emphatically that the city was empty within.
translations.idiomatic: " Prince Xian of Qi and Pillar of State Wang Yi also thought that to leave would surely mean no escape. Duan Chang and others further declared emphatically that the city was empty within.

sentences.zh: 周主乃駐馬，鳴角收兵，俄頃復振。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler thereupon halted his horse, sounded the horn to gather the troops, and in a short while they rallied again.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor thereupon halted his horse, sounded the horn to gather the troops, and in a short while they rallied again.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，旦，還攻東門，克之。

translations.literal: On xinyou, at dawn, they returned to attack the east gate and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, at dawn, they returned to attack the east gate and captured it.

sentences.zh: 延宗戰力屈，走至城北，周人擒之。

translations.literal: Yan Zong's fighting strength was exhausted. He fled to the north of the city and was captured by the Zhou men.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zong's fighting strength was exhausted. He fled to the north of the city and was captured by the Zhou forces.

sentences.zh: 周主下馬執其手，延宗辭曰：「死人手，何敢迫至尊！

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler dismounted and took his hand. Yan Zong declined, saying: "The hand of a dead man—how dare it press upon Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor dismounted and took his hand. Yan Zong declined, saying, "The hand of a dead man—how dare it press upon Your Majesty!

sentences.zh: 」周主曰：「兩國天子，非有怨惡，直為百姓來耳。

translations.literal: " The Zhou ruler said: "The two states' Sons of Heaven bear no mutual hatred. I have come simply for the sake of the people.
translations.idiomatic: " The Zhou emperor said, "The two states' Sons of Heaven bear no mutual hatred. I have come simply for the sake of the people.

sentences.zh: 終不相害，勿怖也。

translations.literal: In the end I will not harm you. Do not be afraid.
translations.idiomatic: In the end I will not harm you. Do not be afraid.

sentences.zh: 」使復衣帽而禮之。

translations.literal: " He had his hat and robes restored and treated him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: " He had his hat and robes restored and treated him with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 唐邕等皆降於周。

translations.literal: Tang Yong and the others all surrendered to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yong and the others all surrendered to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 獨莫多婁敬顯奔鄴，齊主以為司徒。

translations.literal: Only Modou Jingxian fled to Ye. The Qi ruler appointed him Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Only Modou Jingxian fled to Ye. The Northern Qi emperor appointed him Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 延宗初稱尊號，遣使修啟於瀛州刺史任城王湝，曰：「至尊出奔，宗廟事重，群公勸迫，權主號令。

translations.literal: When Yan Zong first assumed the imperial title, he sent envoys with a formal letter to Prince Cheng of Rencheng, Governor of Ying Province, saying: "His Majesty has fled. The altars of state are a weighty matter. The lords pressed me, and I temporarily hold command.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Zong first assumed the imperial title, he sent envoys with a formal letter to Prince Cheng of Rencheng, Governor of Ying Province, saying, "His Majesty has fled. The altars of state are a weighty matter. The lords pressed me, and I temporarily hold command.

sentences.zh: 事寧，終歸叔父。

translations.literal: When affairs are settled, I shall in the end return rule to my uncle.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs are settled, I shall in the end return rule to my uncle.

sentences.zh: 」湝曰：「我人臣，何容受此啟！

translations.literal: " Cheng said: "I am a subject—how can I accept such a letter!
translations.idiomatic: " Cheng said, "I am a subject—how can I accept such a letter!

sentences.zh: 」執使者關送鄴。

translations.literal: " He seized the envoys, put them in confinement, and sent them to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: " He seized the envoys, put them in confinement, and sent them to Ye.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，周主大赦，削除齊制。

translations.literal: On renxu, the Zhou ruler proclaimed a general amnesty and abolished Qi institutions.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, the Zhou emperor proclaimed a general amnesty and abolished Qi institutions.

sentences.zh: 收禮文武之士。

translations.literal: He gathered and honored men of civil and military talent.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered and honored men of civil and military talent.

sentences.zh: 初，鄴伊婁謙聘於齊，其參軍高遵以情輸於齊，齊人拘之於晉陽。

translations.literal: Initially, when Yi Lou Qian of Ye was on a mission to Qi, his staff officer Gao Zun divulged secrets to Qi, and the Qi men detained him at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, when Yi Lou Qian of Ye was on a mission to Qi, his staff officer Gao Zun divulged secrets to Qi, and the Qi forces detained him at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 周主既克晉陽，召謙，勞之。

translations.literal: After the Zhou ruler had captured Jinyang, he summoned Qian and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhou emperor had captured Jinyang, he summoned Qian and comforted him.

sentences.zh: 執遵付謙，任其報復。

translations.literal: He seized Zun and handed him over to Qian, letting him take revenge as he wished.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Zun and handed him over to Qian, letting him take revenge as he wished.

sentences.zh: 謙頓首，請赦之，周主曰：「卿可聚眾唾面，使其知愧。

translations.literal: Qian kowtowed and asked that he be pardoned. The Zhou ruler said: "You may gather the crowd to spit in his face and make him know shame.
translations.idiomatic: Qian kowtowed and asked that he be pardoned. The Zhou emperor said, "You may gather the crowd to spit in his face and make him know shame.

sentences.zh: 」謙曰：「以遵之罪，又非唾面可責。

translations.literal: " Qian said: "For Zun's crime, spitting in the face is not an adequate punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " Qian said, "For Zun's crime, spitting in the face is not an adequate punishment.

sentences.zh: 」帝善其言而止。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved his words and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved his words and stopped.

sentences.zh: 謙待遵如初。

translations.literal: Qian treated Zun as before.
translations.idiomatic: Qian treated Zun as before.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：賞有功，誅有罪，此人君之任也。

translations.literal: Your servant Guang says: To reward merit and punish guilt—this is the ruler's duty.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant Guang says: To reward merit and punish guilt—this is the ruler's duty.

sentences.zh: 高遵奉使異國，漏洩大謀，斯叛臣也。

translations.literal: Gao Zun was sent on a mission to a foreign state and divulged a great plan—he is a traitorous minister.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zun was sent on a mission to a foreign state and divulged a great plan—he is a traitorous minister.

sentences.zh: 周高祖不自行戮，乃以賜謙，使之復怨，失政刑矣！

translations.literal: The Zhou Founding Emperor did not execute him himself but gave him to Qian to let him take revenge—this was a failure of government and punishment!
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou Founding Emperor did not execute him himself but gave him to Qian to let him take revenge—this was a failure of government and punishment!

sentences.zh: 孔子謂以德報怨者，何以報德？

translations.literal: Confucius said: If one repays injury with virtue, with what shall one repay virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: If one repays injury with virtue, with what shall one repay virtue?

sentences.zh: 為謙者，宜辭而不受，歸諸有司，以正典刑。

translations.literal: As for Qian, he should have declined and not accepted him, returning him to the officials to be judged by proper law.
translations.idiomatic: As for Qian, he should have declined and not accepted him, returning him to the officials to be judged by proper law.

sentences.zh: 乃請而赦之以成其私名，美則美矣，亦非公義也。

translations.literal: Instead he asked for pardon and thereby achieved a private reputation for virtue—beautiful though it is, it is not public righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he asked for pardon and thereby achieved a private reputation for virtue—beautiful though it is, it is not public righteousness.

sentences.zh: 齊主命立重賞以募戰士，而竟不出物。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler ordered heavy rewards to recruit warriors, but in the end gave out nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi emperor ordered heavy rewards to recruit warriors, but in the end gave out nothing.

sentences.zh: 廣寧王孝珩請「使任城王湝將幽州道兵入土門，揚聲趣并州，獨孤永業將洛州道兵入潼關，揚聲趣長安，臣請將京畿兵出滏口，鼓行逆戰。

translations.literal: Prince Xiaoheng of Guangning requested: "Let Prince Cheng of Rencheng lead the Youzhou-route troops through Tumen Pass, proclaiming that he is heading for Bing Province; let Dugu Yongye lead the Luozhou-route troops into Tong Pass, proclaiming that he is heading for Chang'an; and let your servant lead the capital-region troops out through Fukou, marching with drums beating to meet the enemy in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiaoheng of Guangning requested, "Let Prince Cheng of Rencheng lead the Youzhou-route troops through Tumen Pass, proclaiming that he is heading for Bing Province; let Dugu Yongye lead the Luozhou-route troops into Tong Pass, proclaiming that he is heading for Chang'an; and let your servant lead the capital-region troops out through Fukou, marching with drums beating to meet the enemy in battle.

sentences.zh: 敵聞南北有兵，自然逃潰。

translations.literal: When the enemy hears that troops are coming from north and south, they will naturally flee and collapse.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy hears that troops are coming from north and south, they will naturally flee and collapse.

sentences.zh: 」又請出宮人珍寶賞將士，齊主不悅。

translations.literal: " He also requested that palace women and treasures be brought out to reward the officers and soldiers. The Qi ruler was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " He also requested that palace women and treasures be brought out to reward the officers and soldiers. The Northern Qi emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 斛律孝卿請齊主親勞將士，為之撰辭，且曰：「宜慷慨流涕，以感激人心。

translations.literal: Hulu Xiaqing asked the Qi ruler to personally comfort the officers and soldiers, composed words for him, and said: "You should speak with generous emotion and shed tears to stir men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Hulu Xiaqing asked the Northern Qi emperor to personally comfort the officers and soldiers, composed words for him, and said, "You should speak with generous emotion and shed tears to stir men's hearts.

sentences.zh: 」齊主既出，臨眾，將令之，不復記所受言，遂大笑，左右亦笑。

translations.literal: " When the Qi ruler came out and faced the crowd, about to give orders, he no longer remembered the words he had been given and burst into laughter. Those around him laughed too.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Northern Qi emperor came out and faced the crowd, about to give orders, he no longer remembered the words he had been given and burst into laughter. Those around him laughed too.

sentences.zh: 將士怒曰：「身尚如此，吾輩何急！

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers said angrily: "If he himself is like this, why should we hurry!
translations.idiomatic: The officers and soldiers said angrily, "If he himself is like this, why should we hurry!

sentences.zh: 」皆無戰心。

translations.literal: " None had any will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: " None had any will to fight.

sentences.zh: 於是自大丞相已下，太宰、三師、大司馬、大將軍、三公等官，並增員而授，或三或四，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Thereupon, from the Grand Chancellor downward, the offices of Grand Mentor, Three Preceptors, Grand Marshal, Grand General, Three Dukes, and the like were all increased in number and filled—some with three or four appointees, beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon, from the Grand Chancellor downward, the offices of Grand Mentor, Three Preceptors, Grand Marshal, Grand General, Three Dukes, and the like were all increased in number and filled—some with three or four appointees, beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 朔州行台僕射高勱將兵侍衛太后、太子，自土門道還鄴。

translations.literal: Gao Mai, Vice Director of the Shuozhou Executive, led troops escorting the Empress Dowager and Crown Prince back to Ye by the Tumen route.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Mai, Vice Director of the Shuozhou Executive, led troops escorting the Empress Dowager and Crown Prince back to Ye by the Tumen route.

sentences.zh: 時宦官儀同三司苟子溢猶恃寵縱暴，民間雞彘，縱鷹犬搏噬取之；

translations.literal: At the time the eunuch Palace Gate General of the Third Rank Gou Ziyi still relied on favor to act violently. Chickens and pigs among the people—he let his hawks and dogs seize and devour them;
translations.idiomatic: At the time the eunuch Palace Gate General of the Third Rank Gou Ziyi still relied on favor to act violently. Chickens and pigs among the people—he let his hawks and dogs seize and devour them;

sentences.zh: 勱執以徇，將斬之；

translations.literal: Mai seized him and displayed him for execution, about to behead him;
translations.idiomatic: Mai seized him and displayed him for execution, about to behead him;

sentences.zh: 太后救之，得免。

translations.literal: the Empress Dowager rescued him, and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: the Empress Dowager rescued him, and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 或謂勱曰：「子溢之徒，言成禍福，獨不慮後患邪？

translations.literal: Someone said to Mai: "Men like Ziyi can by a word bring fortune or disaster—do you alone not consider future trouble?
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Mai, "Men like Ziyi can by a word bring fortune or disaster—do you alone not consider future trouble?

sentences.zh: 」勱攘袂曰：「今西寇已據并州，達官率皆委叛，正坐此輩濁亂朝廷。

translations.literal: " Mai rolled up his sleeves and said: "Now the western invaders already hold Bing Province, and high officials are mostly deserting and rebelling. It is precisely because of men like these befouling and disordering the court.
translations.idiomatic: " Mai rolled up his sleeves and said, "Now the western invaders already hold Bing Province, and high officials are mostly deserting and rebelling. It is precisely because of men like these befouling and disordering the court.

sentences.zh: 若得今日斬之，明日受誅，亦無所恨！

translations.literal: If I can behead him today and be executed myself tomorrow, I shall have no regret!
translations.idiomatic: If I can behead him today and be executed myself tomorrow, I shall have no regret!

sentences.zh: 」勱，岳之子也。

translations.literal: " Mai was the son of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: " Mai was the son of Yue.

sentences.zh: 甲子，齊太后至鄴。

translations.literal: On jiazi, the Qi Empress Dowager reached Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, the Qi Empress Dowager reached Ye.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，周主出齊宮中珍寶服玩及宮女二千人，班賜將士，加立功者官爵各有差。

translations.literal: On bingyin, the Zhou ruler brought out treasures, robes, playthings, and two thousand palace women from the Qi palace and distributed them to the officers and soldiers. Those who had rendered merit received additional ranks and titles according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, the Zhou emperor brought out treasures, robes, playthings, and two thousand palace women from the Qi palace and distributed them to the officers and soldiers. Those who had rendered merit received additional ranks and titles according to merit.

sentences.zh: 周主問高延宗以取鄴之策，辭曰：「此非亡國之臣所及。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler asked Gao Yan Zong for a plan to take Ye. He declined, saying: "This is not within the reach of a minister of a fallen state.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor asked Gao Yan Zong for a plan to take Ye. He declined, saying, "This is not within the reach of a minister of a fallen state.

sentences.zh: 」強問之，乃曰：「若任城工據鄴，臣不能知。

translations.literal: " When pressed, he finally said: "If Prince Cheng holds Ye, your servant cannot know.
translations.idiomatic: " When pressed, he finally said, "If Prince Cheng holds Ye, your servant cannot know.

sentences.zh: 若今主自守，陛下兵不血刃。

translations.literal: If the present ruler holds it himself, Your Majesty's army will take it without bloodshed.
translations.idiomatic: If the present ruler holds it himself, Your Majesty's army will take it without bloodshed.

sentences.zh: 」癸酉，周師趣鄴，命齊王憲先驅，以上柱國陳王純為并州總管。

translations.literal: " On guiyou the Zhou army pressed toward Ye. Prince Xian of Qi was ordered to lead the vanguard, and Upper Pillar of State Prince Chun of Chen was made overall commander of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: " On guiyou the Zhou army pressed toward Ye. Prince Xian of Qi was ordered to lead the vanguard, and Upper Pillar of State Prince Chun of Chen was made overall commander of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 齊主引諸貴臣入朱雀門，賜酒食，問以御周之策，人人異議，齊主不知所從。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler led the various high ministers into Vermilion Bird Gate, bestowed wine and food, and asked them for plans to resist Zhou. Each man had a different opinion, and the Qi ruler did not know whom to follow.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi emperor led the various high ministers into Vermilion Bird Gate, bestowed wine and food, and asked them for plans to resist Zhou. Each man had a different opinion, and the Northern Qi emperor did not know whom to follow.

sentences.zh: 是時人情恟懼，莫有鬥心，朝士出降，晝夜相屬。

translations.literal: At this time men's hearts were alarmed and fearful; none had the will to fight. Court officials went out to surrender day and night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: At this time men's hearts were alarmed and fearful; none had the will to fight. Court officials went out to surrender day and night without cease.

sentences.zh: 高勱曰：「今之叛者，多是貴人，至於卒伍，猶未離心。

translations.literal: Gao Mai said: "Those who rebel now are mostly men of rank. As for the common soldiers, their hearts have not yet turned away.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Mai said, "Those who rebel now are mostly men of rank. As for the common soldiers, their hearts have not yet turned away.

sentences.zh: 請追五品已上家屬，置之三台，因脅之以戰，若不捷，則焚台。

translations.literal: I request that the families of officials of the fifth rank and above be seized and placed in Santai. Then force them to fight. If we do not succeed, burn the tower.
translations.idiomatic: I request that the families of officials of the fifth rank and above be seized and placed in Santai. Then force them to fight. If we do not succeed, burn the tower.

sentences.zh: 此曹顧惜妻子，必當死戰。

translations.literal: These men, cherishing their wives and children, will surely fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: These men, cherishing their wives and children, will surely fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 且王師頻北，賊徒輕我，今背城一決，理必破之。

translations.literal: Moreover the royal army has repeatedly gone north, and the bandits despise us. If we now stake all with our backs to the city, reason says we must break them.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the royal army has repeatedly gone north, and the bandits despise us. If we now stake all with our backs to the city, reason says we must break them.

sentences.zh: 」齊主不能用。

translations.literal: " The Qi ruler could not adopt this plan.
translations.idiomatic: " The Northern Qi emperor could not adopt this plan.

sentences.zh: 望氣者言，當有革易。

translations.literal: A reader of cosmic signs said there would be a change of dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: A reader of cosmic signs said there would be a change of dynasty.

sentences.zh: 齊主引尚書令高元海等議，依天統故事，禪位皇太子。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler summoned Chief Minister of State Affairs Gao Yuanhai and others to discuss following the precedent of the Tiantong reign and abdicating in favor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi emperor summoned Chief Minister of State Affairs Gao Yuanhai and others to discuss following the precedent of the Tiantong reign and abdicating in favor of the Crown Prince.
